title.zh: 卷八十五 志第三十八 地理一
title.raw: 卷八十五 志第三十八 地理一 Volume 85 Treatises 38: Geography 1

sentences.zh: 京城京畿路京東路京西路

translations.literal: Capital City; Jingji Circuit; Jingdong Circuit; Jingxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Capital City; Jingji Circuit; Jingdong Circuit; Jingxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 唐室既衰，五季迭興，五十餘年，更易八姓，宇縣分裂，莫之能一。

translations.literal: The house of Tang had already declined; the Five Dynasties arose in succession; in more than fifty years eight surnames were exchanged; the counties of the realm split apart, and none could unify them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang dynasty fell into decline, the Five Dynasties arose one after another; in a little more than fifty years eight ruling houses succeeded one another, and the realm fractured so that none could reunite it.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖受周禪，初有州百一十一，縣六百三十八，戶九十六萬七千三百五十三。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Song received the abdication of Zhou; at first there were 111 prefectures, 638 counties, and 967,353 households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Song received the throne by abdication from the Later Zhou, the realm initially comprised 111 prefectures, 638 counties, and 967,353 registered households.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，取荊南，得州、府三江陵府，歸、峽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, he took Jingnan and gained three prefectures and one superior prefecture: Jiangling Superior Prefecture, Gui, and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong (963), he conquered Jingnan, gaining three prefectures plus Jiangling Superior Prefecture, Gui, and Xia.

sentences.zh: ，縣一十七，戶一十四萬二千三百。

translations.literal: , seventeen counties, and 142,300 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added seventeen counties and 142,300 households.

sentences.zh: 平湖南，得州一十五、監一潭、衡、邵、郴、道、永、全、嶽、澧、朗、蔣、辰、錦、溪、敘，桂陽監

translations.literal: Pacifying southern Hunan, he gained fifteen prefectures and one supervisory commission: Tan, Heng, Shao, Chen, Dao, Yong, Quan, Yue, Li, Lang, Jiang, Chen, Jin, Xi, and Xu, and the Guiyang Supervisory Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying southern Hunan, he gained fifteen prefectures and one supervisory commission—Tan, Heng, Shao, Chen, Dao, Yong, Quan, Yue, Li, Lang, Jiang, Chen, Jin, Xi, and Xu—as well as the Guiyang Supervisory Commission.

sentences.zh: ，縣六十六，戶九萬七千三百八十八。

translations.literal: , sixty-six counties, and 97,388 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added sixty-six counties and 97,388 households.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，平蜀，得州、府四十六益、彭、眉、嘉、邛、蜀、綿、漢、資、簡、梓、黎、雅、陵、戎、瀘、維、茂、昌、榮、果、閬、渠、合、龍、普、利、興、文、巴、劍、蓬、壁、夔、忠、萬、集、開、渝、涪、黔、施、達、洋，興元府

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, he pacified Shu and gained forty-six prefectures and one superior prefecture: Yi, Peng, Mei, Jia, Qiong, Shu, Mian, Han, Zi, Jian, Zi, Li, Ya, Ling, Rong, Lu, Wei, Mao, Chang, Rong, Guo, Lang, Qu, He, Long, Pu, Li, Xing, Wen, Ba, Jian, Peng, Bi, Kui, Zhong, Wan, Ji, Kai, Yu, Fu, Qian, Shi, Da, Yang, and Xingyuan Superior Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande (965), he pacified Shu, gaining forty-six prefectures plus Xingyuan Superior Prefecture—among them Yi, Peng, Mei, Jia, Qiong, Shu, Mian, Han, Zi, Jian, Zi, Li, Ya, Ling, Rong, Lu, Wei, Mao, Chang, Rong, Guo, Lang, Qu, He, Long, Pu, Li, Xing, Wen, Ba, Jian, Peng, Bi, Kui, Zhong, Wan, Ji, Kai, Yu, Fu, Qian, Shi, Da, and Yang.

sentences.zh: ，縣一百九十八，戶五十三萬四千三十九。

translations.literal: , 198 counties, and 534,039 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added 198 counties and 534,039 households.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，平廣南，得州六十廣、韶、潮、循、封、端、英、連、雄、龔、惠、康、恩、春、瀧、勤、新、高、潘、雷、羅、辨、桂、賀、昭、梧、蒙、恭、象、富、融、宜、柳、嚴、思唐、邕、澄、貴、蠻、橫、賓、欽、潯、容、牢、白、廉、黨、繡、郁林、藤、竇、義、禺、順、瓊、崖、儋、萬安、振

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, he pacified Guangnan and gained sixty prefectures: Guang, Shao, Chao, Xun, Feng, Duan, Ying, Lian, Xiong, Gong, Hui, Kang, En, Chun, Long, Qin, Xin, Gao, Pan, Lei, Luo, Bian, Gui, He, Zhao, Wu, Meng, Gong, Xiang, Fu, Rong, Yi, Liu, Yan, Sitang, Yong, Cheng, Gui, Man, Heng, Bin, Qin, Xun, Rong, Lao, Bai, Lian, Dang, Xiu, Yulin, Teng, Dou, Yi, Yu, Shun, Qiong, Ya, Dan, Wan'an, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao (971), he pacified Guangnan, gaining sixty prefectures including Guang, Shao, Chao, Xun, Feng, Duan, Ying, Lian, Xiong, Gong, Hui, Kang, En, Chun, Long, Qin, Xin, Gao, Pan, Lei, Luo, Bian, Gui, He, Zhao, Wu, Meng, Gong, Xiang, Fu, Rong, Yi, Liu, Yan, Sitang, Yong, Cheng, Gui, Man, Heng, Bin, Qin, Xun, Rong, Lao, Bai, Lian, Dang, Xiu, Yulin, Teng, Dou, Yi, Yu, Shun, Qiong, Ya, Dan, Wan'an, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: ，縣二百一十四，戶一十七萬二百六十三。

translations.literal: , 214 counties, and 170,263 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added 214 counties and 170,263 households.

sentences.zh: 八年，平江南，得州一十九，軍三升、宣、歙、池、洪、潤、常、鄂、筠、饒、信、虔、吉、袁、撫、江、汀、建、劍、江陰、雄遠、建昌軍

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he pacified Jiangnan and gained nineteen prefectures and three armies: Sheng, Xuan, She, Chi, Hong, Run, Chang, E, Jun, Rao, Xin, Qian, Ji, Yuan, Fu, Jiang, Ting, Jian, Jian, Jiangyin, Xiongyuan, and Jianchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (975), he pacified Jiangnan, gaining nineteen prefectures and three armies—Sheng, Xuan, She, Chi, Hong, Run, Chang, E, Jun, Rao, Xin, Qian, Ji, Yuan, Fu, Jiang, Ting, Jian, and Jian—along with the Jiangyin, Xiongyuan, and Jianchang armies.

sentences.zh: ，縣一百八，戶六十五萬五千六十五。

translations.literal: , 108 counties, and 655,065 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added 108 counties and 655,065 households.

sentences.zh: 計其末年，凡有州二百九十七，縣一千八十六，戶三百九萬五百四。

translations.literal: Calculating to his final year, in all there were 297 prefectures, 1,186 counties, and 3,090,504 households.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of his reign, the realm altogether comprised 297 prefectures, 1,186 counties, and 3,090,504 households.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國三年，陳洪進獻地，得州二，漳、泉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo under Emperor Taizong, Chen Hongjin presented his territory and two prefectures were gained: Zhang and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo (978), Chen Hongjin surrendered his domain, adding the two prefectures of Zhang and Quan.

sentences.zh: 縣十四，戶十五萬一千九百七十八。

translations.literal: Fourteen counties and 151,978 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added fourteen counties and 151,978 households.

translations.literal: Qian Chu
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu

sentences.zh: 入朝，得州十三、軍一杭、蘇、越、湖、衢、婺、台、明、溫、秀、睦、福、處，衣錦。

translations.literal: came to court and thirteen prefectures and one army were gained: Hang, Su, Yue, Hu, Qu, Wu, Tai, Ming, Wen, Xiu, Mu, Fu, Chu, and the Yijin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, the realm gained thirteen prefectures and one army—Hang, Su, Yue, Hu, Qu, Wu, Tai, Ming, Wen, Xiu, Mu, Fu, and Chu—along with the Yijin Army.

sentences.zh: ，縣八十六，戶五十五萬六百八十。

translations.literal: , eighty-six counties, and 550,680 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added eighty-six counties and 550,680 households.

sentences.zh: 四年，平太原，得州十、軍一併、汾、嵐、憲、忻、代、遼、沁、隆、石，寶興。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Taiyuan was pacified and ten prefectures and one army were gained: Bing, Fen, Lan, Xian, Xin, Dai, Liao, Qin, Long, Shi, and the Baoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (979), Taiyuan was pacified, adding ten prefectures—Bing, Fen, Lan, Xian, Xin, Dai, Liao, Qin, Long, and Shi—along with the Baoxing Army.

sentences.zh: ，縣四十，戶三萬五千二百二十。

translations.literal: , forty counties, and 35,220 households.
translations.idiomatic: This added forty counties and 35,220 households.

sentences.zh: 七年，李繼捧來朝，得州四夏、銀、綏、宥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Li Jipeng came to court and four prefectures were gained: Xia, Yin, Sui, and You.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (982), Li Jipeng came to court, and the realm gained the four northwestern prefectures of Xia, Yin, Sui, and You.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，復以四州授繼捧，自後不復領于職方

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, the four prefectures were again granted to Jipeng; thereafter they were no longer administered by the Directorate of Administrative Maps
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi (984), the four prefectures were restored to Jipeng; thereafter they were no longer listed under the Directorate of Administrative Maps

translations.literal: , eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: —eight counties in all.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，天下上閏年圖，州、府、軍、監幾於四百

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, the empire submitted the intercalary-year map; prefectures, superior prefectures, armies, and supervisory commissions numbered nearly four hundred
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, the empire submitted its intercalary-year territorial map; prefectures, superior prefectures, armies, and supervisory commissions together numbered nearly four hundred

sentences.zh: 至是，天下既一，疆理幾復漢、唐之舊，其未入職方氏者，唯燕、雲十六州而已。

translations.literal: By this time the realm was already unified; its boundaries nearly restored those of Han and Tang; what had not entered the registers of the Directorate of Administrative Maps was only the sixteen prefectures of Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was united, and its boundaries nearly matched those of Han and Tang; only the sixteen Yan–Yun prefectures still lay outside the Directorate's registers.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，分天下為十五路，天聖析為十八，元豐又析為二十三：曰京東東、西，曰京西南、北，曰河北東、西，曰永興，曰秦鳳，曰河東，曰淮南東、西，曰兩浙，曰江南東、西，曰荊湖南、北，曰成都，曰梓、利、夔、曰福建，曰廣南東、西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, the realm was divided into fifteen circuits; in Tiansheng it was split into eighteen, and in Yuanfeng again into twenty-three: called Jingdong East and West, Jingxi Southwest and North, Hebei East and West, Yongxing, Qinfeng, Hedong, Huainan East and West, Liangzhe, Jiangnan East and West, Jinghu South and North, Chengdu, Zi, Li, and Kui, Fujian, and Guangnan East and West.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao (997) the realm was divided into fifteen circuits; under Tiansheng this became eighteen, and under Yuanfeng twenty-three: Jingdong East and West; Jingxi Southwest and North; Hebei East and West; Yongxing; Qinfeng; Hedong; Huainan East and West; Liangzhe; Jiangnan East and West; Jinghu South and North; Chengdu; Zi, Li, and Kui; Fujian; and Guangnan East and West.

sentences.zh: 東南際海，西盡巴僰，北極三關，東西六千四百八十五里，南北萬一千六百二十里。

translations.literal: Southeast it reached the sea; west it extended to Ba and Bo; north it reached the Three Passes; east to west 6,485 li; north to south 11,620 li.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast it reached the sea; to the west it extended to Ba and Bo; to the north it reached the Three Passes; it measured 6,485 li from east to west and 11,620 li from north to south.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning, the Jingji Circuit was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongning (1105), the Jingji Circuit was re-established.

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, the Qiannan Circuit was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan (1107), the Qiannan Circuit was established as a separate administrative unit.

sentences.zh: 三年，並黔南入廣西，以廣西黔南為名。

translations.literal: In the third year, Qiannan was merged into Guangxi and named Guangxi-Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1109), Qiannan was merged into Guangxi and the combined circuit was styled Guangxi-Qiannan.

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it reverted to being Guangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1110), it reverted to the former name of Guangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 當是時，天下有戶二千八十八萬二千二百五十八，口四千六百七十三萬四千七百八十四天下主客戶：自至道末四百一十三萬一千五百七十六，天禧五年，主戶六百三萬九千三百三十一，客戶不預焉。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had 20,882,258 households and 46,734,784 persons. Households throughout the realm, principal and guest: from the end of Zhidao 4,131,576; in the fifth year of Tianxi, principal households 6,393,331; guest households were not included.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm registered 20,882,258 households and 46,734,784 persons. For principal and guest households empire-wide: at the end of Zhidao there were 4,131,576; in the fifth year of Tianxi (1021) there were 6,393,331 principal households, guest households not being counted.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐八年，主戶一千二百四十六萬二千五百三十一，口二千六百四十二萬一千六百五十一。

translations.literal: By the eighth year of Jiayou, principal households numbered 12,462,531 and persons 26,421,651.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth year of Jiayou (1063), principal households numbered 12,462,531 and persons 26,421,651.

sentences.zh: 至治平三年，天下主客戶一千四百一十八萬一千四百八十六，口二千五十萬六千九百八十。

translations.literal: By the third year of Zhiping, principal and guest households throughout the realm numbered 14,181,486 and persons 20,506,980.
translations.idiomatic: By the third year of Zhiping (1066), principal and guest households empire-wide numbered 14,181,486 and persons 20,506,980.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，戶一千四百二十四萬五千二百七十，口三千八十萬七千二百十一。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, households numbered 14,245,270 and persons 30,807,211.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xining (1077), households numbered 14,245,270 and persons 30,807,211.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，戶一千七百九十五萬七千九十二，口四千七萬二千六百六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, households numbered 17,957,092 and persons 40,072,606.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou (1086), households numbered 17,957,092 and persons 40,072,606.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，戶一千九百一十二萬九百二十一，口四千二百五十六萬六千二百四十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, households numbered 19,120,921 and persons 42,566,243.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng (1094), households numbered 19,120,921 and persons 42,566,243.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，戶一千九百九十六萬八百一十二，口四千四百九十一萬四千九百九十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, households numbered 19,960,812 and persons 44,914,991.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfu (1100), households numbered 19,960,812 and persons 44,914,991.

sentences.zh: 崇甯元年，戶二千二十六萬四千三百七，口四千五百三十二萬四千一百五十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, households numbered 20,264,307 and persons 45,324,154.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning (1102), households numbered 20,264,307 and persons 45,324,154.

sentences.zh: 各府、州下戶口與總數少異，姑兩存之

translations.literal: The household figures under each superior prefecture and prefecture differ slightly from the totals; for the present both are retained
translations.idiomatic: The household figures listed under individual superior prefectures and prefectures differ slightly from the empire-wide totals; both figures are retained for now

translations.literal: , and compared with the height of Western Han there was probably an increase.
translations.idiomatic: , exceeding even the peak population of Western Han.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐疆理雖廣，而戶口皆有所不及。

translations.literal: Although the boundaries of Sui and Tang were broad, in households and persons both fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Although Sui and Tang ruled vast territories, their registered populations fell short of this.

sentences.zh: 迨宣和四年，又置燕山府及雲中府路，天下分路二十六，京府四，府三十，州二百五十四，監六十三，縣一千二百三十四，可謂極盛矣。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Xuanhe, Yanshan Superior Prefecture and the Yunzhong Superior Prefecture Circuit were again established; the realm was divided into twenty-six circuits, four capital superior prefectures, thirty superior prefectures, 254 prefectures, 63 supervisory commissions, and 1,234 counties—this may be called the utmost flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year of Xuanhe (1122), Yanshan Superior Prefecture and the Yunzhong Superior Prefecture Circuit had been added; the realm comprised twenty-six circuits, four capital superior prefectures, thirty superior prefectures, 254 prefectures, 63 supervisory commissions, and 1,234 counties—the empire at its zenith.

sentences.zh: 大抵宋有天下三百餘年，繇建隆初訖治平末，一百四年，州郡沿革無大增損。

translations.literal: In general Song held the realm for more than three hundred years; from the beginning of Jianlong to the end of Zhiping, 104 years, in the evolution of prefectures and commanderies there was no great increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the Song held the realm for more than three hundred years; from the beginning of Jianlong through the end of Zhiping—a span of 104 years—prefectural boundaries changed little.

sentences.zh: 熙寧始務辟土，而種諤先取綏州，韓絳繼取銀州，王韶取熙河，章惇取懿、洽，謝景溫取徽、誠，熊本取南平，郭逵取廣源，最後李憲取蘭州，沈括取葭蘆、米脂、浮圖、安疆等砦。

translations.literal: From Xining they began to devote themselves to opening territory: Zhong E first took Sui Prefecture; Han Jiang then took Yin Prefecture; Wang Shao took Xihe; Zhang Dun took Yi and Qia; Xie Jingwen took Hui and Cheng; Xiong Ben took Nanping; Guo Kui took Guangyuan; finally Li Xian took Lan Prefecture; Shen Kuo took the stockades of Jialu, Mizhi, Futuo, Anjiang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xining the court turned to territorial expansion: Zhong E first seized Sui Prefecture; Han Jiang followed with Yin; Wang Shao took Xihe; Zhang Dun took Yi and Qia; Xie Jingwen took Hui and Cheng; Xiong Ben took Nanping; Guo Kui took Guangyuan; finally Li Xian took Lanzhou, and Shen Kuo seized the stockades of Jialu, Mizhi, Futuo, Anjiang, and others.

sentences.zh: 雖嘗以河東邊界七百里地與遼人，當時王安石議，蓋曰：「吾將取之，甯姑與之也。」

translations.literal: Although they once ceded seven hundred li of Hedong borderland to the Liao, at the time Wang Anshi argued, saying in effect: "I am going to take it; I would rather give it away for the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Although seven hundred li of Hedong borderland were once ceded to the Liao, Wang Anshi argued at the time that it was better to yield ground temporarily: "We mean to take it back; we might as well let them hold it for now."

sentences.zh: 迨元祐更張，葭蘆等四砦給賜夏人，而分畫久不能定。

translations.literal: When Yuanyou reversed course, the four stockades of Jialu and the rest were granted to the Xia, and the demarcation long could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanyou the policy was reversed: the four stockades including Jialu were granted to the Western Xia, and the border demarcation remained unsettled for years.

sentences.zh: 紹聖遂罷分畫，督諸路各乘勢攻討進築。

translations.literal: Under Shaosheng they then abolished demarcation and urged each circuit to seize the moment to attack, pursue, and advance construction.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaosheng demarcation talks were abandoned, and each circuit was ordered to press attacks and advance fortified positions wherever opportunity allowed.

sentences.zh: 自三年秋八月訖元符二年冬，凡陝西、河東建州一安西

translations.literal: From the eighth month of autumn in the third year until the winter of the second year of Yuanfu, in Shaanxi and Hedong altogether one prefecture was established: Anxi
translations.idiomatic: From the eighth month of autumn in the third year of Shaosheng through the winter of the second year of Yuanfu (1099), in Shaanxi and Hedong the court established one prefecture—Anxi

translations.literal: , two armies: Jinning and Suide
translations.idiomatic: , two armies—Jinning and Suide

translations.literal: , three passes: Longping, Huining, and Jincheng
translations.idiomatic: , three passes—Longping, Huining, and Jincheng

sentences.zh: ，城九安西，平夏、威戎、興平、定邊、威羌、金湯、白豹、會川

translations.literal: , nine walled cities: Anxi, Pingxia, Weirong, Xingping, Dingbian, Weiqiang, Jintang, Baibao, and Huichuan
translations.idiomatic: , nine walled cities—Anxi, Pingxia, Weirong, Xingping, Dingbian, Weiqiang, Jintang, Baibao, and Huichuan

sentences.zh: ，砦二十八平羌、平戎、殄羌、暖泉、米脂、克戎、安疆、橫山、綏遠、寧羌、靈平、高平、西平、新泉、蕩羌、通峽、天都、臨羌、定戎、龕穀、大和、通秦、寧河、彌川、寧遠、神泉、烏龍

translations.literal: , twenty-eight stockades: Pingqiang, Pingrong, Tianqiang, Nuanquan, Mizhi, Kerong, Anjiang, Hengshan, Suiyuan, Ningqiang, Lingping, Gaoping, Xiping, Xinquan, Dangqiang, Tongxia, Tiandu, Linqiang, Dingrong, Kangu, Dahe, Tongqin, Ninghe, Michuan, Ningyuan, Shenquan, and Wulong
translations.idiomatic: , twenty-eight stockades—Pingqiang, Pingrong, Tianqiang, Nuanquan, Mizhi, Kerong, Anjiang, Hengshan, Suiyuan, Ningqiang, Lingping, Gaoping, Xiping, Xinquan, Dangqiang, Tongxia, Tiandu, Linqiang, Dingrong, Kangu, Dahe, Tongqin, Ninghe, Michuan, Ningyuan, Shenquan, and Wulong

sentences.zh: ，堡十開光、通塞、石門、通會、大和、通秦、寧河、彌川、寧川、三交，又取青唐鄯。

translations.literal: , ten forts: Kaiguang, Tongsai, Shimen, Tonghui, Dahe, Tongqin, Ninghe, Michuan, Ningchuan, and Sanjiao; they also took Qingtang and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: , ten forts—Kaiguang, Tongsai, Shimen, Tonghui, Dahe, Tongqin, Ninghe, Michuan, Ningchuan, and Sanjiao—and also seized Qingtang and Shan.

translations.literal: , Miaochuan, Huang.
translations.idiomatic: , Miaochuan, and Huang.

translations.literal: , Ningsai, and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: , Ningsai, and Kuo.

translations.literal: , Longzhi, and Zongge
translations.idiomatic: , Longzhi, and Zongge

translations.literal: and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: and other cities.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國悉還吐蕃故壤，稍紓民力。

translations.literal: In Jianzhong Jingguo all the former Tibetan lands were returned, slightly easing the burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong Jingguo the court returned the former Tibetan territories, bringing modest relief to the populace.

sentences.zh: 崇寧亟變前議，專以紹述為事，蔡京始任童貫、王厚，更取湟、鄯、廓三州二十餘壘。

translations.literal: Chongning swiftly changed the earlier policy and devoted itself solely to continuing the former reign's undertakings; Cai Jing first entrusted Tong Guan and Wang Hou, and again took the three prefectures of Huang, Shan, and Kuo and more than twenty fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning the court quickly reversed prior policy, dedicating itself to reviving the late Shenzong's programs; Cai Jing placed Tong Guan and Wang Hou in command and recovered Huang, Shan, and Kuo along with more than twenty fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 陶節夫、鐘傳、刑恕、胡宗回、曾孝序之徒，又相與鑿空駕虛，馳騖于元符封域之表。

translations.literal: Tao Jiefu, Zhong Chuan, Xing Shu, Hu Zonghui, Zeng Xiaoxu, and their kind again together carved emptiness and rode on voidness, racing beyond the borders fixed in Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jiefu, Zhong Chuan, Xing Shu, Hu Zonghui, Zeng Xiaoxu, and others pressed reckless campaigns far beyond the borders established under Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 訖於重和，既立靖夏涇原

translations.literal: Down to Chonghe, they had already established Jingxia in Jingyuan Circuit
translations.idiomatic: By Chonghe the court had established Jingxia in Jingyuan Circuit

translations.literal: , Zhirong in Fuyan Circuit
translations.idiomatic: , Zhirong in Fuyan Circuit

translations.literal: , and Zhiqiang in Xining Circuit
translations.idiomatic: , and Zhiqiang in Xining Circuit

sentences.zh: 三城，雖夏人浸衰，而民力亦弊。

translations.literal: three cities; although the Xia people gradually declined, the people's strength was also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: three fortified cities; though the Western Xia gradually weakened, the populace was worn down as well.

translations.literal: The western affair had just been settled when northern trouble swiftly arose.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the western campaigns subsided when trouble erupted in the north.

sentences.zh: 蓋自崇寧以來，益、梓、夔、黔、廣西、荊湖南、北迭相視效，斥大土宇，靡有寧歲，凡所建州、軍、關、城、砦、堡，紛然莫可勝紀。

translations.literal: From Chongning onward, Yi, Zi, Kui, Qian, Guangxi, and Jinghu South and North circuits emulated one another in turn, extending territory greatly; there was scarcely a peaceful year; all the prefectures, armies, passes, cities, stockades, and forts established were so numerous they could not be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongning onward the Yi, Zi, Kui, Qian, Guangxi, and Jinghu South and North circuits emulated one another in territorial expansion, leaving scarcely a year of peace; the prefectures, armies, passes, cities, stockades, and forts they established were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 厥後建燕山、雲中兩路，粗閱三歲，禍變旋作，中原板蕩，故府淪沒，職方所記，漫不可考。

translations.literal: Thereafter the two circuits of Yanshan and Yunzhong were established; in barely three years calamity swiftly arose; the Central Plains were thrown into turmoil; former prefectures were lost; what the Directorate of Administrative Maps recorded became hopelessly unverifiable.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Yanshan and Yunzhong circuits were established; within barely three years disaster struck, the Central Plains were thrown into chaos, former prefectures fell, and the Directorate's records became impossible to verify.

sentences.zh: 高宗蒼黃渡江，駐蹕吳會，中原、陝右盡入于金，東畫長淮，西割商、秦之半，以散關為界，其所存者，兩浙、兩淮、江東西、湖南北、西蜀、福建、廣東、廣西十五路而已，有戶一千二百六十六萬九千六百八十四此甯宗嘉定十一年數

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong in haste crossed the Yangzi and halted at Wu and Kuai; the Central Plains and Shaanxi west all entered Jin; east they drew the Long Huai as boundary; west they cut off half of Shang and Qin, taking San Pass as the border; what remained were only the fifteen circuits of Liangzhe, Lianghuai, Jiangdong and Jiangxi, Hunan and Hubei, Western Shu, Fujian, Guangdong, and Guangxi; there were 12,669,684 households—this is the figure for the eleventh year of Jiading under Emperor Ningzong
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong fled south across the Yangzi in haste and established his court at Wu and Kuai; the Central Plains and western Shaanxi fell entirely to the Jin; to the east the Long Huai became the border, to the west half of Shang and Qin were lost with San Pass as the frontier; only fifteen circuits remained—Liangzhe, Lianghuai, Jiangdong and Jiangxi, Hunan and Hubei, Western Shu, Fujian, Guangdong, and Guangxi—with 12,669,684 households, the figure for the eleventh year of Jiading under Emperor Ningzong (1218)

sentences.zh: 建國江左又百五十年，迨德祐丙子，遂並歸於我皇元版圖，而天下始復合為一焉。

translations.literal: Establishing the state on the left bank of the Yangzi for another hundred and fifty years, by the bingzi year of Deyou it all returned to the territory of our August Yuan, and the realm at last was reunited as one.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty ruled south of the Yangzi for another century and a half; by the bingzi year of Deyou (1276) all fell within the dominion of our Great Yuan, and the realm was united once more.

sentences.zh: 今據元豐所定，並京畿為二十四路，首之以京師，重帝都也。

translations.literal: Now according to the Yuanfeng demarcation, together with Jingji there are twenty-four circuits; the capital is placed first, honoring the imperial metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: The present account follows the Yuanfeng demarcation: with Jingji included there are twenty-four circuits, opening with the capital to honor the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 終之以燕、雲，以其既得而旋失，故附見於後。

translations.literal: It ends with Yan and Yun, because they were gained and soon lost, and so are appended at the rear.
translations.idiomatic: It closes with Yan and Yun, territories briefly recovered and soon lost again, and therefore treated in an appendix.

sentences.zh: 而凡四京之城闕宮室，及南渡行在之所，其可考者冠乎篇首，為《地理志》雲。

translations.literal: As for the city walls and palaces of the Four Capitals, and the places of the southern crossing where the mobile court resided, what can be verified is placed at the head of the chapter—thus the Treatise on Geography.
translations.idiomatic: The city walls and palaces of the Four Capitals, together with the southern capital where the court resided after the crossing—whatever can be verified—is placed at the head of this chapter: thus begins the Treatise on Geography.

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was Kaifeng of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital was Kaifeng on the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 梁為東都，後唐罷，晉復為東京，宋因周之舊為都，建隆三年，廣皇城東北隅，命有司畫洛陽宮殿，按圖修之，皇居始壯麗矣。

translations.literal: Liang made it the Eastern Capital; Later Tang abolished it; Jin again made it the Eastern Capital; Song followed Zhou's precedent as capital; in the third year of Jianlong the northeast corner of the Imperial City was expanded; officials were ordered to draw the Luoyang palaces and repair according to the plans—the imperial residence first became grand.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang made it their eastern capital; the Later Tang abandoned it; the Later Jin restored it as the Eastern Capital; the Song retained Zhou's capital at Kaifeng. In the third year of Jianlong (962) the northeast corner of the Imperial City was enlarged; officials were ordered to draft plans from the Luoyang palaces and rebuild accordingly—the imperial residence first attained its full splendor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，欲廣宮城，詔殿前指揮使劉延翰等經度之，以居民多不欲徙，遂罷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, wishing to enlarge the palace city, the emperor ordered Palace Front Commander Liu Yanhan and others to survey it; because many residents were unwilling to relocate, the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi (986), planning to enlarge the palace city, the emperor ordered Palace Front Commander Liu Yanhan and others to survey the site; because many residents refused to relocate, the project was abandoned.

translations.literal: The palace city measured five li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city measured five li in circumference.

translations.literal: ; east was called the Left Flank Gate, west the Right Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: ; to the east was the Left Flank Gate, to the west the Right Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 東西面門曰東華、西華舊名寬仁、神獸，開寶三年改今名。

translations.literal: The east and west face gates were called Donghua and Xihua; formerly named Kuanren and Shenshou; in the third year of Kaibao they were changed to the present names.
translations.idiomatic: The east and west face gates were Donghua and Xihua, formerly Kuanren and Shenshou; in the third year of Kaibao (970) they received their present names.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，又改東華門北曰謻門

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, north of Donghua Gate was again renamed Yimen Gate
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xining (1077), the gate north of Donghua Gate was renamed Yimen Gate

sentences.zh: ，北一門曰拱宸舊名玄武，大中祥符五年改今名，熙寧十年，改門內西橫門曰臨華

translations.literal: ; one northern gate was called Gongchen, formerly named Xuanwu; in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu it was changed to the present name; in the tenth year of Xining the western transverse gate inside the gate was renamed Linhua
translations.idiomatic: ; the northern gate was Gongchen, formerly Xuanwu, renamed in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1012); in the tenth year of Xining (1077) the western transverse gate within it was renamed Linhua

sentences.zh: 乾元門內正南門曰大慶，東、西橫門曰左、右升龍。

translations.literal: Inside Qianyuan Gate the main southern gate was called Daqing; the east and west transverse gates were called Left and Right Ascending Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Qianyuan Gate the main southern gate was Daqing; the east and west transverse gates were the Left and Right Ascending Dragon gates.

sentences.zh: 左右北門內各二門，曰左、右長慶熙寧間，改左、右長慶隔門曰左、右嘉肅

translations.literal: Inside the left and right northern gates were two gates each, called Left and Right Changqing; during Xining the Left and Right Changqing partition gates were changed to Left and Right Jiashu
translations.idiomatic: Within each of the left and right northern gates were two inner gates, the Left and Right Changqing; during Xining the partition gates of Left and Right Changqing were renamed Left and Right Jiashu

translations.literal: , and Left and Right Yintai.
translations.idiomatic: , and the Left and Right Yintai gates.

sentences.zh: 東華門內一門曰左承天祥符乾德六年賜名，大中祥符元年正月，天書降其上，詔加「祥符」二字而增茸之

translations.literal: Inside Donghua Gate one gate was called Left Chengtian Xiangfu; in the sixth year of Qiande of the Xiangfu era it was granted its name; in the first month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu a celestial book descended upon it; an edict added the two characters "Xiangfu" and enlarged and repaired it
translations.idiomatic: Inside Donghua Gate stood one gate called Left Chengtian Xiangfu, granted its name in the sixth year of Qiande under the Xiangfu reign title; in the first month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008) a celestial book descended upon it, and an edict added the characters "Xiangfu" and ordered the gate enlarged and restored

sentences.zh: 西華門內一門曰右承天。

translations.literal: Inside Xihua Gate one gate was called Right Chengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Xihua Gate stood one gate called Right Chengtian.

sentences.zh: 左承天門內道北門曰宣祐舊名光天，大中祥符八年改大寧，明道元年改今名

translations.literal: Inside Left Chengtian Gate on the north of the inner passage was a gate called Xuanyou; formerly named Guangtian; in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu changed to Daning; in the first year of Mingdao changed to the present name
translations.idiomatic: North along the inner passage from Left Chengtian Gate stood Xuanyou Gate, formerly Guangtian, renamed Daning in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1015) and given its present name in the first year of Mingdao (1032)

sentences.zh: 正南門內正殿曰大慶，東、西門曰左、右太和宋初曰日華、月華，大中祥符八年改今名

translations.literal: Inside the main southern gate the main hall was called Daqing; the east and west gates were called Left and Right Taihe; in early Song called Rihua and Yuehua; in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu changed to the present names
translations.idiomatic: Within the main southern gate the principal hall was Daqing; the east and west gates were the Left and Right Taihe gates, called Rihua and Yuehua in early Song until renamed in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1015)

sentences.zh: 大慶殿舊名崇元，乾德四年重修，改曰乾元，太平興國九年改朝元，大中祥符八年改天安，明道三年改今名

translations.literal: Daqing Hall was formerly named Chongyuan; in the fourth year of Qiande it was rebuilt and renamed Qianyuan; in the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo renamed Chaoyuan; in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu renamed Tian'an; in the third year of Mingdao renamed to the present name
translations.idiomatic: Daqing Hall was formerly Chongyuan; rebuilt in the fourth year of Qiande (966) and renamed Qianyuan; renamed Chaoyuan in the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo (984), Tian'an in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1015), and given its present name in the third year of Mingdao (1032)

sentences.zh: 北有紫宸殿舊名崇德，明道元年改

translations.literal: To the north was Zichen Hall, formerly named Chongde; renamed in the first year of Mingdao
translations.idiomatic: To the north stood Zichen Hall, formerly Chongde, renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032)

translations.literal: , the front hall for holding court.
translations.idiomatic: , the front hall where the emperor held court.

sentences.zh: 西有垂拱殿舊名長春，明道元年改。

translations.literal: To the west was Chuigong Hall, formerly named Changchun; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood Chuigong Hall, formerly Changchun, renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

translations.literal: It was the place for daily court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: This was where the emperor held court on ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 次西有皇儀殿開寶四年，賜名滋福，明道元年十月改。

translations.literal: Next west was Huangyi Hall; in the fourth year of Kaibao it was granted the name Zifu; in the tenth month of the first year of Mingdao it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Next to the west stood Huangyi Hall, granted the name Zifu in the fourth year of Kaibao (971) and renamed in the tenth month of the first year of Mingdao (1032).

sentences.zh: ，又次西有集英殿舊名廣政，開寶三年曰大明，淳化間曰含光，大中祥符八年名會慶，明道元年十月改今名。

translations.literal: , and next further west was Jiying Hall, formerly named Guangzheng; in the third year of Kaibao called Daming; in the Chunhua era called Hanguang; in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu named Huiqing; in the tenth month of the first year of Mingdao changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: , and still farther west stood Jiying Hall, formerly Guangzheng, called Daming in the third year of Kaibao (970), Hanguang during the Chunhua era (978–983), Huiqing in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1015), and given its present name in the tenth month of the first year of Mingdao (1032).

translations.literal: It was a banquet hall.
translations.idiomatic: It served as a banquet hall.

sentences.zh: 殿后有需雲殿舊名玉華，後改瓊華，熙甯初改今名。

translations.literal: Behind the hall was Xuyun Hall, formerly named Yuhua, later changed to Qionghua; at the beginning of Xining changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the hall stood Xuyun Hall, formerly Yuhua and later Qionghua, given its present name at the beginning of the Xining era (1068).

sentences.zh: 東有升平樓舊名紫雲，明道元年改。

translations.literal: To the east was Shengping Tower, formerly named Ziyun; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood Shengping Tower, formerly Ziyun, renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

translations.literal: It was the place within the palace for viewing banquets.
translations.idiomatic: This was where banquets were viewed within the palace.

sentences.zh: 宮後有崇政殿舊名簡賢講武，太平興國二年改今名。

translations.literal: Behind the palace was Chongzheng Hall, formerly named Jianxian Jiangwu; in the second year of Taiping Xingguo changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the palace stood Chongzheng Hall, formerly Jianxian Jiangwu, renamed in the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977).

sentences.zh: 熙寧間，改北橫門曰通極。

translations.literal: During the Xining era, the North Horizontal Gate was renamed Tongji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era (1068–1077), the North Horizontal Gate was renamed Tongji.

translations.literal: It was the place for reviewing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This was where affairs were reviewed.

sentences.zh: 殿后有景福殿，殿西有殿北向，曰延和，便坐殿也大中祥符七年，建後苑東門，洎北向便殿成，賜名宣和門、承明殿，明道元年改端明，二年改今名。

translations.literal: Behind the hall was Jingfu Hall; west of the hall was a hall facing north called Yanhe, also an informal seating hall; in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu the eastern gate of the rear garden was built; when the north-facing informal hall was completed, granted the names Xuanhe Gate and Chengming Hall; in the first year of Mingdao renamed Duanming; in the second year changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the hall stood Jingfu Hall; west of the hall was a north-facing hall called Yanhe, also used as an informal seating hall; in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1014) the eastern gate of the rear garden was built, and when the north-facing informal hall was completed it was granted the names Xuanhe Gate and Chengming Hall; in the first year of Mingdao (1032) it was renamed Duanming, and in the second year given its present name.

translations.literal: Whenever a hall had a gate, all followed the hall's name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a hall had a gate, the gate took the hall's name.

sentences.zh: 宮中又有延慶、舊名萬歲，大中祥符七年改。

translations.literal: Within the palace there were also Yanqing, formerly named Wansui; changed in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace were also Yanqing Hall, formerly Wansui, renamed in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1014).

sentences.zh: 安福、觀文、舊名集聖，明道二年改肅儀，慶曆八年改今名。

translations.literal: Anfu, Guanwen, formerly named Jisheng; in the second year of Mingdao renamed Suyi; in the eighth year of Qingli changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Anfu and Guanwen halls—the latter formerly Jisheng, renamed Suyi in the second year of Mingdao (1033) and given its present name in the eighth year of Qingli (1048).

sentences.zh: 清景、慶雲、玉京等殿，壽寧堂舊名清淨，明道元年改。

translations.literal: Qingjing, Qingyun, Yujing, and other halls; Shouning Hall was formerly named Qingjing; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Qingjing, Qingyun, Yujing, and other halls; Shouning Hall was formerly Qingjing, renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

translations.literal: Yanchun Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchun Pavilion.

translations.literal: Formerly named Wanchun; renamed in the first year of Baoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wanchun, renamed in the first year of Baoyuan (1038).

sentences.zh: 福甯殿即延慶，明道元年改。

translations.literal: Funing Hall was Yanqing; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: Funing Hall was the same as Yanqing, renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

translations.literal: To east and west were gates called Left and Right Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: To the east and west were gates called the Left and Right Zhaoqing gates.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿西門曰延真，其東真君殿曰積慶，前建感真閣。

translations.literal: The west gate of Guanwen Hall was called Yanzhen; east of it Zhenjun Hall was called Jiqing; in front was built Gazhen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The west gate of Guanwen Hall was Yanzhen; east of it stood Zhenjun Hall, called Jiqing, with Gazhen Pavilion built in front.

sentences.zh: 又有龍圖閣，下有資政、崇和、宣德、述古殿。

translations.literal: There was also Longtu Pavilion, below which were Zizheng, Chonghe, Xuande, and Shugu halls.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Longtu Pavilion, beneath which stood the Zizheng, Chonghe, Xuande, and Shugu halls.

sentences.zh: 天章閣下有群玉、蕊珠二殿，後有寶文閣，即壽昌閣，慶曆元年改。

translations.literal: Below Tianzhang Pavilion were Qunyu and Ruizhu halls; behind was Baowen Pavilion, formerly Shouchang Pavilion; renamed in the first year of Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath Tianzhang Pavilion were the Qunyu and Ruizhu halls; behind stood Baowen Pavilion, formerly Shouchang Pavilion, renamed in the first year of Qingli (1041).

sentences.zh: 閣東西有嘉德、延康二殿，前有景輝門。

translations.literal: East and west of the pavilion were Jiade and Yankang halls; in front was Jinghui Gate.
translations.idiomatic: East and west of the pavilion were the Jiade and Yankang halls, with Jinghui Gate in front.

sentences.zh: 後苑東門曰甯陽，即宣和門，明道元年改。

translations.literal: The eastern gate of the rear garden was called Ningyang, that is, Xuanhe Gate; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern gate of the rear garden was Ningyang—that is, Xuanhe Gate—renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

sentences.zh: 苑內有崇聖殿、太清樓，其西又有宜聖、化成、即玉宸殿，明道元年改。

translations.literal: Within the garden were Chongsheng Hall and Taiqing Tower; further west were also Yisheng and Huacheng, that is, Yuchen Hall; renamed in the first year of Mingdao.
translations.idiomatic: Within the garden stood Chongsheng Hall and Taiqing Tower; farther west were also Yisheng and Huacheng halls—the latter being Yuchen Hall—renamed in the first year of Mingdao (1032).

sentences.zh: 金華、西涼、清心等殿，翔鸞、儀鳳二閣，華景、翠芳、瑤津三亭。

translations.literal: Jinhua, Xiliang, Qingxin, and other halls; Xiangluan and Yifeng pavilions; Huajing, Cuifang, and Yaojin pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: There were Jinhua, Xiliang, Qingxin, and other halls; the Xiangluan and Yifeng pavilions; and the Huajing, Cuifang, and Yaojin pavilions.

sentences.zh: 延福宮有穆清殿，延慶殿北有柔儀殿，初有殿無名，章獻太后名曰崇徽，明道元年改寶慈，景祐二年改今名。

translations.literal: Yanfu Palace had Muhui Hall; north of Yanqing Hall was Rouyi Hall; at first there was a hall without a name; Empress Dowager Zhangxian named it Chonghui; in the first year of Mingdao renamed Baoci; in the second year of Jingyou changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu Palace contained Muhui Hall; north of Yanqing Hall stood Rouyi Hall, which at first had no name until Empress Dowager Zhangxian named it Chonghui; it was renamed Baoci in the first year of Mingdao (1032) and given its present name in the second year of Jingyou (1035).

translations.literal: North of Chonghui Hall was Qinming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: North of Chonghui Hall stood Qinming Hall.

sentences.zh: 舊名天和，明道元年改觀文，又改清居，治平三年改今名。

translations.literal: Formerly named Tianhe; in the first year of Mingdao renamed Guanwen; again renamed Qingju; in the third year of Zhiping changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tianhe, renamed Guanwen in the first year of Mingdao (1032), then Qingju, and given its present name in the third year of Zhiping (1066).

sentences.zh: 延福宮北有廣聖宮，天聖二年建，名長寧，

translations.literal: North of Yanfu Palace was Guangsheng Palace, built in the second year of Tiansheng, named Changning,
translations.idiomatic: North of Yanfu Palace stood Guangsheng Palace, built in the second year of Tiansheng (1024) and named Changning,

translations.literal: changed in the second year of Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: renamed in the second year of Jingyou (1035).

sentences.zh: 內有太清、玉清、沖和、集福、會祥五殿，建流杯殿于後苑。

translations.literal: Within were Taiqing, Yuqing, Chonghe, Jifu, and Huixiang halls; Liubei Hall was built in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were the Taiqing, Yuqing, Chonghe, Jifu, and Huixiang halls; Liubei Hall was built in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 明道元年八月，修文德殿成。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Mingdao, Wenwude Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Mingdao (1032), Wenwude Hall was completed.

sentences.zh: 是夜，禁中火，延燔崇德、長春、滋福、會慶、延慶、崇徽、天和、承明八殿，命宰相呂夷簡為修茸大內使，樞密副使楊崇勳副之，發京東西、河北、淮南、江東西路工匠給役，內出乘輿物，左藏庫易緡錢二十萬助其費，以故改諸殿名。

translations.literal: That night fire broke out in the forbidden quarter and spread to burn the eight halls Chongde, Changchun, Zifu, Huiqing, Yanqing, Chonghui, Tianhe, and Chengming; the chancellor Lü Yijian was appointed commissioner for repairing the inner palace, with Vice Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Chongxun as his deputy; craftsmen were dispatched from the Jingdong, Jingxi, Hebei, Huainan, Jiangdong, and Jiangxi circuits for service; imperial carriages and goods were issued from within; twenty thousand strings of cash from the Left Repository were exchanged to assist the expense; for this reason the various halls were renamed.
translations.idiomatic: That night a fire broke out in the forbidden quarter and spread to consume eight halls—Chongde, Changchun, Zifu, Huiqing, Yanqing, Chonghui, Tianhe, and Chengming. Chancellor Lü Yijian was appointed commissioner for repairing the inner palace, with Vice Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Chongxun as his deputy; artisans were summoned from the Jingdong, Jingxi, Hebei, Huainan, Jiangdong, and Jiangxi circuits; imperial carriages and furnishings were issued from within, and twenty thousand strings of cash from the Left Repository were provided toward the cost—hence the renaming of the various halls.

sentences.zh: 又有慈德殿，楊太后所居，景祐元年賜名。

translations.literal: There was also Cide Hall, where Empress Dowager Yang resided; the name was granted in the first year of Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cide Hall, residence of Empress Dowager Yang, granted its name in the first year of Jingyou (1034).

sentences.zh: 觀稼殿，在後苑，觀種稻，景祐二年創建。

translations.literal: Guanjia Hall, in the rear garden, for viewing rice cultivation; established in the second year of Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: Guanjia Hall stood in the rear garden for viewing rice cultivation; it was established in the second year of Jingyou (1035).

translations.literal: Yanyi Pavilion, west of Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi Pavilion lay west of Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 邇英閣，在崇政殿西南，蓋侍臣講讀之所也，與延義同，景祐三年賜名。

translations.literal: Erying Pavilion, southwest of Chongzheng Hall, was where attending ministers lectured and read; the same as Yanyi; the name was granted in the third year of Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: Erying Pavilion, southwest of Chongzheng Hall, was where attending ministers lectured and read—the same function as Yanyi—and received its name in the third year of Jingyou (1036).

sentences.zh: 隆儒殿，邇英閣後小殿，皇祐三年始賜名。

translations.literal: Longru Hall, a small hall behind Erying Pavilion; the name was first granted in the third year of Huangyou.
translations.idiomatic: Longru Hall was a small hall behind Erying Pavilion; its name was first granted in the third year of Huangyou (1051).

sentences.zh: 慈壽殿，皇太后所居，治平元年賜名。

translations.literal: Cishou Hall, where the empress dowager resided; the name was granted in the first year of Zhiping.
translations.idiomatic: Cishou Hall was the empress dowager's residence; its name was granted in the first year of Zhiping (1064).

sentences.zh: 慶壽宮，保慈宮，熙寧二年建。

translations.literal: Qingshou Palace and Baoci Palace, built in the second year of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshou Palace and Baoci Palace were built in the second year of Xining (1069).

translations.literal: Yuhua Hall, in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhua Hall stood in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 基春殿，熙寧七年建，在玉華殿后。

translations.literal: Jichun Hall, built in the seventh year of Xining, behind Yuhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jichun Hall was built in the seventh year of Xining (1074), behind Yuhua Hall.

translations.literal: Ruisi Hall, built in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Ruisi Hall was built in the eighth year [of Xining, 1075].

translations.literal: Chengji Hall, built in the third year of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chengji Hall was built in the third year of Yuanfeng (1080).

sentences.zh: 崇慶、隆祐二宮，元祐元年建。

translations.literal: Chongqing and Longyou palaces, built in the first year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing and Longyou palaces were built in the first year of Yuanyou (1086).

sentences.zh: 睿成宮，神宗所居東宮，紹聖二年賜名。

translations.literal: Ruicheng Palace, the Eastern Palace where Shenzong resided; the name was granted in the second year of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng Palace was the Eastern Palace where Shenzong had resided; its name was granted in the second year of Shaosheng (1095).

sentences.zh: 宣和殿，在睿思殿后，紹聖二年四月殿成，其東側別有小殿曰凝芳，其西曰瓊芳，前曰重熙，後曰環碧。

translations.literal: Xuanhe Hall, behind Ruisi Hall; in the fourth month of the second year of Shaosheng the hall was completed; on its east side were separate small halls called Ningfang; on the west Qiongfang; in front Chongxi; behind Huanbi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhe Hall stood behind Ruisi Hall; the hall was completed in the fourth month of the second year of Shaosheng (1095). On its east were separate small halls called Ningfang; on the west, Qiongfang; in front, Chongxi; behind, Huanbi.

sentences.zh: 元符三年廢，崇甯初復作，大觀三年，徽宗制記刻石，實蔡京為之。

translations.literal: Abolished in the third year of Yuanfu; restored at the beginning of Chongning; in the third year of Daguan, Huizong composed an inscription carved on stone, but in fact Cai Jing wrote it.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in the third year of Yuanfu (1100), restored at the beginning of Chongning (1102), and in the third year of Daguan (1109) Huizong had an inscription carved in stone—though in fact Cai Jing composed it.

sentences.zh: 聖瑞宮，皇太妃所居，因以名宮。

translations.literal: Shengrui Palace, where the imperial noble consort resided; the palace was named accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Shengrui Palace housed the imperial noble consort, and the palace was named for that purpose.

sentences.zh: 顯謨閣，元符元年建，藏神宗禦集，建中靖國元年，改曰熙明，尋復舊。

translations.literal: Xianmo Pavilion, built in the first year of Yuanfu, storing Shenzong's collected writings; in the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo renamed Ximing; soon restored to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: Xianmo Pavilion was built in the first year of Yuanfu (1098) to house Shenzong's collected writings; in the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo (1101) it was renamed Ximing, but soon reverted to its former name.

translations.literal: Yuxu Hall, built at the beginning of Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxu Hall was built at the beginning of the Yuanfu era (1098).

sentences.zh: 玉華閣，大觀初建，在宣和殿后。

translations.literal: Yuhua Pavilion, built at the beginning of Daguan, behind Xuanhe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhua Pavilion was built at the beginning of the Daguan era (1107), behind Xuanhe Hall.

translations.literal: Qincan Palace, built in the first year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Qincan Palace was built in the first year of Zhenghe (1111).

sentences.zh: 燕寧殿，在延福北，奉安仁宗慈聖光獻皇后御容。

translations.literal: Yanning Hall, north of Yanfu, enshrining the imperial portrait of Empress Cisheng Guangxian of Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanning Hall, north of Yanfu, enshrined the imperial portrait of Empress Cisheng Guangxian of Renzong.

sentences.zh: 延福宮，政和三年春，新作於大內北拱辰門外。

translations.literal: Yanfu Palace, in the spring of the third year of Zhenghe, newly built outside the north Gongchen Gate of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu Palace was newly built in the spring of the third year of Zhenghe (1113), outside the inner palace's north Gongchen Gate.

sentences.zh: 舊宮在後苑之西南，今其地乃百司供應之所，凡內酒坊、裁造院、油醋柴炭鞍轡等庫，悉移它處，又遷兩僧寺、兩軍營，而作新宮焉。

translations.literal: The old palace was in the southwest of the rear garden; its site became the supply depot of the hundred offices; all the inner wine workshops, tailoring directorates, oil, vinegar, charcoal, saddle, and bridle storehouses, and the like were moved elsewhere; two Buddhist temples and two military camps were also relocated, and the new palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: The old palace had stood in the southwest of the rear garden; its site became quarters for the supply services of the hundred offices—the inner wine workshops, tailoring directorate, and storehouses for oil, vinegar, charcoal, saddles, bridles, and the like were all moved elsewhere, as were two Buddhist temples and two military camps, and the new palace was erected in their place.

sentences.zh: 始南向，殿因宮名曰延福，次曰蕊珠，有亭曰碧琅玕。

translations.literal: At first it faced south; the hall took the palace name Yanfu; next was Ruizhu; there was a pavilion called Bilanggan.
translations.idiomatic: At first it faced south; the main hall took the palace name Yanfu; next came Ruizhu; and there was a pavilion called Bilanggan.

sentences.zh: 其東門曰晨暉，其西門曰麗澤。

translations.literal: Its east gate was called Chenhui; its west gate was called Lize.
translations.idiomatic: Its east gate was Chenhui; its west gate was Lize.

translations.literal: To the left of the palace two sections were again arranged.
translations.idiomatic: To the palace's left two sections were again laid out.

sentences.zh: 其殿則有穆清、成平、會寧、睿謨、凝和、昆玉，群玉，其東閣則有蕙馥

translations.literal: Its halls were Muhui, Chengping, Huining, Ruimo, Ninghe, Kunyu, and Qunyu; its eastern pavilions included Huifu
translations.idiomatic: Its halls were Muhui, Chengping, Huining, Ruimo, Ninghe, Kunyu, and Qunyu; its eastern pavilions included Huifu

sentences.zh: 、報瓊、蟠桃、春錦、疊瓊、芬芳、麗玉、寒香、拂雲、偃蓋、翠葆、鉛英、雲錦、蘭薰、摘金，其西閣有繁英、雪香、披芳、鉛華、瓊華、文綺、絳萼、穠華、綠綺、瑤碧、清陰、秋香、叢玉、扶玉、絳雲、會寧之北，疊石為山，山上有殿曰翠微，旁為二亭：曰雲巋，曰層巘。

translations.literal: , Baojiong, Pantao, Chunjin, Dieqiong, Fenfang, Liyu, Hanxiang, Fuyun, Yangai, Cuibao, Qianying, Yunjin, Lanxun, and Zhaijin; its western pavilions included Fanying, Xuexiang, Pifang, Qianhua, Qionghua, Wenqi, Jiang'e, Nonghua, Lüqi, Yaobi, Qingyin, Qiuxiang, Congyu, Fuyu, and Jiangyun; north of Huining, stones were piled into a mountain, with a hall on the mountain called Cuwei and two pavilions beside it called Yunkui and Cengyan.
translations.idiomatic: , Baojiong, Pantao, Chunjin, Dieqiong, Fenfang, Liyu, Hanxiang, Fuyun, Yangai, Cuibao, Qianying, Yunjin, Lanxun, and Zhaijin; its western pavilions included Fanying, Xuexiang, Pifang, Qianhua, Qionghua, Wenqi, Jiang'e, Nonghua, Lüqi, Yaobi, Qingyin, Qiuxiang, Congyu, Fuyu, and Jiangyun. North of Huining, stones were piled into a mountain with a hall atop it called Cuwei and two flanking pavilions called Yunkui and Cengyan.

sentences.zh: 凝和之次閣曰明春，其高逾一百一十尺。

translations.literal: The pavilion next to Ninghe was called Mingchun; its height exceeded one hundred and ten chi.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion next to Ninghe was Mingchun, rising more than one hundred and ten chi.

sentences.zh: 閣之側為殿二：曰玉英，曰玉澗。

translations.literal: Beside the pavilion were two halls: called Yuying and Yujian.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the pavilion stood two halls called Yuying and Yujian.

sentences.zh: 其背附城，築土植杏，名杏岡，覆茅為亭，修竹萬竿，引流其下。

translations.literal: Its back adjoined the city wall; earth was piled and apricots planted, named Apricot Mound; thatched pavilions were roofed; ten thousand bamboo poles; water was channeled below.
translations.idiomatic: Its rear adjoined the city wall; earth was heaped and apricots planted to form the Apricot Mound, thatched pavilions were built, ten thousand bamboo poles set out, and a stream led beneath them.

sentences.zh: 宮之右為佐二閣，曰宴春，廣十有二丈，舞臺四列，山亭三峙。

translations.literal: To the right of the palace were two auxiliary pavilions called Yanchun, twelve zhang wide, with four rows of dance platforms and three mountain pavilions standing.
translations.idiomatic: To the palace's right stood two auxiliary pavilions called Yanchun, twelve zhang wide, with four rows of dance platforms and three mountain pavilions rising above.

sentences.zh: 鑿圓池為海，跨海為二亭，架石樑以升山，亭曰飛華，橫度之四百尺有奇，縱數之二百六十有七尺。

translations.literal: A circular pool was carved as a sea; spanning the sea were two pavilions; a stone bridge was erected to ascend the mountain; the pavilion was called Feihua; its width was four hundred odd chi; its length two hundred sixty-seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: A circular pool was carved out as a sea, with two pavilions spanning it; a stone bridge led up the mountain to Feihua Pavilion, more than four hundred chi across and two hundred sixty-seven chi long.

sentences.zh: 又疏泉為湖，湖中作堤以接亭，堤中作梁以通湖，梁之上又為茅亭、鶴莊、鹿砦、孔翠諸柵，蹄尾動數千，嘉花名木，類聚區別，幽勝宛若生成，西抵麗澤，不類塵境。

translations.literal: A stream was also opened into a lake; within the lake a dike was made to reach the pavilion; within the dike a bridge was made to cross the lake; atop the bridge were again thatched pavilions, Crane Lodge, Deer Enclosure, and pens for peacocks and kingfishers; hooves and tails numbered in the thousands; fine flowers and famous trees were gathered and distinguished; secluded beauty seemed naturally formed; westward to Lize, unlike the dusty world.
translations.idiomatic: Streams were also opened into a lake, with a dike within the lake reaching the pavilion and a bridge within the dike crossing the water; atop the bridge stood thatched pavilions, Crane Lodge, Deer Enclosure, and aviaries for peacocks and kingfishers—hoofed and tailed creatures numbering in the thousands; choice flowers and celebrated trees were gathered and sorted by kind; the secluded splendor seemed wrought by nature itself; westward to Lize Gate it was unlike the dusty world outside.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡京命童貫、楊戩、賈詳、藍從熙、何䐶等分任宮役，五人者因各為制度，不務沿襲，故號「延福五位」。

translations.literal: At first Cai Jing ordered Tong Guan, Yang Kai, Jia Xiang, Lan Congxi, He Chong, and others to divide the palace work; the five men each made their own design, not following precedent; hence they were called the "Yanfu Five Positions."
translations.idiomatic: At first Cai Jing assigned Tong Guan, Yang Kai, Jia Xiang, Lan Congxi, He Chong, and others to divide the palace work among them; the five men each devised his own design without following precedent, hence the name "Yanfu Five Positions."

translations.literal: East and west matched the inner palace; north and south were slightly inferior.
translations.idiomatic: East and west it matched the inner palace in scale; north and south it was somewhat smaller.

sentences.zh: 其東直景龍門，西抵天波門，宮東西二橫門，皆視禁門法，所謂晨暉、麗澤者也，而晨暉門出入最多。

translations.literal: East it reached Jinglong Gate; west it reached Tianbo Gate; the palace's east and west horizontal gates both followed the regulations for forbidden gates—the so-called Chenhui and Lize—and Chenhui Gate had the most traffic.
translations.idiomatic: To the east it ran straight to Jinglong Gate; to the west it reached Tianbo Gate. The palace's east and west horizontal gates both followed the regulations for forbidden gates—the Chenhui and Lize gates—and Chenhui Gate saw the heaviest traffic.

sentences.zh: 其後又跨舊城修築，號「延福第六位」。

translations.literal: Later it was again built spanning the old city, called the "Yanfu Sixth Position."
translations.idiomatic: Later construction again spanned the old city wall, called the "Yanfu Sixth Position."

sentences.zh: 跨城之外浚壕，深者水三尺，東景龍門橋，西天波門橋，二橋之下疊石為固，引舟相通，而橋上人物外自通行不覺也，名曰景龍江。

translations.literal: Outside the span a moat was dredged; where deepest the water was three chi; east was Jinglong Gate Bridge, west Tianbo Gate Bridge; below the two bridges stones were piled solid; boats were led to pass through; yet people and goods above passed outward and inward without noticing; it was named Jinglong River.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the span a moat was dredged, three chi deep at its deepest; east stood Jinglong Gate Bridge and west Tianbo Gate Bridge, with stone piled solid beneath both so boats could pass through while people and goods above came and went unawares—the waterway was named Jinglong River.

sentences.zh: 其後又辟之，東過景龍門至封丘門。

translations.literal: Later it was again opened; east past Jinglong Gate to Fengqiu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was opened farther still, east past Jinglong Gate to Fengqiu Gate.

translations.literal: North of Jinglong River was Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: North of Jinglong River stood Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 初，元符三年，以懿親宅潛邸為之，及作景龍江，江夾岸皆奇花珍木，殿宇比比對峙，中途曰壺春堂，絕岸至龍德宮。

translations.literal: At first, in the third year of Yuanfu, the hidden residence of an imperial kinsman was made into it; when Jinglong River was built, both banks were lined with rare flowers and precious trees, halls and towers facing one another in pairs; midway was Huchun Hall, reaching the far bank to Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the third year of Yuanfu (1100), an imperial kinsman's hidden residence was converted into it; when Jinglong River was constructed, both banks were planted with rare flowers and precious trees, halls and towers rising face to face; midway stood Huchun Hall, spanning the far bank to Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 其地歲時次第展拓，後盡都城一隅焉，名曰擷芳園，山水美秀，林麓暢茂，樓觀參差，猶艮嶽、延福也。

translations.literal: The territory was expanded year by year in sequence; later it encompassed an entire corner of the capital; named Jiefang Garden; mountains and waters beautiful and fine; forests and foothills luxuriant; towers and halls rising in tiers; like Genyue and Yanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The grounds were expanded year by year until they eventually occupied an entire corner of the capital, named Jiefang Garden—its mountains and waters fair, its woods and slopes lush, its towers and halls rising in tiers, rivaling Genyue and Yanfu.

translations.literal: The palace was in the old city; therefore it is appended here.
translations.idiomatic: The palace lay in the old city; it is therefore appended here.

sentences.zh: 保和殿，政和三年四月作，九月殿成，總為屋七十五間。

translations.literal: Baohe Hall, made in the fourth month of the third year of Zhenghe; in the ninth month the hall was completed; seventy-five bays in all.
translations.idiomatic: Baohe Hall was begun in the fourth month of the third year of Zhenghe (1113); the hall was completed in the ninth month, seventy-five bays in all.

sentences.zh: 玉清神霄宮，政和三年建，舊名玉清和陽，在福寧殿東，七年改今名。

translations.literal: Yuqing Shenxiao Palace, built in the third year of Zhenghe, formerly named Yuqing Heyang, east of Funing Hall; in the seventh year changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing Shenxiao Palace was built in the third year of Zhenghe (1113), formerly Yuqing Heyang, east of Funing Hall; in the seventh year (1117) it received its present name.

sentences.zh: 上清寶陰宮，政和五年作，在景龍門東，對景暉門。

translations.literal: Shangqing Baoyin Palace, built in the fifth year of Zhenghe, east of Jinglong Gate, facing Jinghui Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shangqing Baoyin Palace was built in the fifth year of Zhenghe (1115), east of Jinglong Gate, facing Jinghui Gate.

sentences.zh: 既又作仁濟、輔正二亭于宮前，命道士施民符藥，徽宗時登皇城下視之。

translations.literal: Then again the Renji and Fuzheng pavilions were built before the palace; Daoist priests were ordered to give the people talismans and medicine; Huizong often ascended the imperial city walls to look down.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Renji and Fuzheng pavilions were built before the palace, and Daoist priests were ordered to distribute talismans and medicine to the people while Huizong often mounted the imperial city walls to look down.

sentences.zh: 又開景龍門，城上作復道，通寶陰宮，以便齋醮之路，徽宗數從復道上往來。

translations.literal: Jinglong Gate was also opened; on the wall an elevated passage was built connecting to Baoyin Palace to facilitate the route for fasting and offerings; Huizong often traveled back and forth on the elevated passage.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong Gate was also opened, and an elevated passage was built atop the wall to Baoyin Palace to ease the route for fasting rites; Huizong often traveled back and forth along it.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，始張燈于景龍門上下，名曰「預賞」。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, lanterns were first displayed above and below Jinglong Gate, called "Preview Enjoyment."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year lanterns were first displayed above and below Jinglong Gate in what was called the "Preview Enjoyment."

translations.literal: The following year, then came the affair of the Qimen guards.
translations.idiomatic: The following year brought the affair of the Qimen guards.

translations.literal: Wansui Mountain Genyue.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui Mountain and Genyue.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，始於上清寶籙宮之東作萬歲山。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, Wansui Mountain was first built east of Shangqing Baolu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenghe (1117), construction of Wansui Mountain began east of Shangqing Baolu Palace.

sentences.zh: 山周十餘里，其最高一峰九十步，上有亭曰介，分東、西二嶺，直接南山。

translations.literal: The mountain's circuit was over ten li; its highest peak ninety steps; atop it was a pavilion called Jie; it divided into east and west ridges, connecting directly to the south mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain's circuit exceeded ten li; its highest peak rose ninety steps, with a pavilion called Jie atop it; it divided into east and west ridges running straight to the south mountain.

sentences.zh: 山之東有萼綠華堂，有書館、八仙館、紫石岩、棲真嶝、覽秀軒、龍吟堂。

translations.literal: East of the mountain was Elühua Hall, with a library, Baxian Lodge, Zishi Rock, Qizhen Ridge, Lanxiu Pavilion, and Longyin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountain stood Elühua Hall, along with a library, Baxian Lodge, Zishi Rock, Qizhen Ridge, Lanxiu Pavilion, and Longyin Hall.

sentences.zh: 山之南則壽山兩峰並峙，有雁池、噰噰亭，北直絳霄樓。

translations.literal: South of the mountain two peaks of Shoushan stood side by side, with Yan Pool and Yongyong Pavilion; north straight to Jiangxiao Tower.
translations.idiomatic: South of the mountain the two peaks of Shoushan stood side by side, with Yan Pool and Yongyong Pavilion; northward they ran straight to Jiangxiao Tower.

sentences.zh: 山之西有藥寮，有西莊，有巢雲亭，有白龍沜、濯龍峽，蟠秀、練光、跨雲亭，羅漢岩。

translations.literal: West of the mountain was a medicine lodge, Xizhuang, Chaoyun Pavilion, Bailong Marsh, Zhuolong Gorge, Panxiu, Lianguang, and Kuayun pavilions, and Luohan Rock.
translations.idiomatic: West of the mountain were a medicine lodge, Xizhuang, Chaoyun Pavilion, Bailong Marsh, Zhuolong Gorge, and the Panxiu, Lianguang, and Kuayun pavilions, as well as Luohan Rock.

sentences.zh: 又西有萬松嶺，半嶺有樓曰倚翠，上下設兩關，關下有平地，鑿大方沼，中作兩洲：東為蘆渚，亭曰浮陽。

translations.literal: Farther west was Wansong Ridge; halfway up the ridge was a tower called Yicui; above and below were two passes; below the passes was level ground; a large square marsh was carved; within were made two islets: east was Luzhu, the pavilion Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Farther west lay Wansong Ridge; halfway up stood Yicui Tower, with two passes above and below; below the passes was level ground where a large square marsh was carved, containing two islets—east was Luzhu, with Fuyang Pavilion.

translations.literal: West was Meizhu; the pavilion Xuelang.
translations.idiomatic: West was Meizhu, with Xuelang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 西流為鳳池，東出為雁池，中分二館，東曰流碧，西曰環山，有閣曰巢鳳，堂曰三秀，東池後有揮雪廳。

translations.literal: Flowing west was Feng Pool; flowing east was Yan Pool; within were divided two lodges: east called Liubi; west called Huanshan; there was a pavilion Chaofeng; a hall Sanxiu; behind the east pool was Huixue Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing west was Feng Pool and east Yan Pool; within were two lodges—east, Liubi; west, Huanshan—with Chaofeng Pavilion, Sanxiu Hall, and behind the east pool Huixue Hall.

sentences.zh: 復由嶝道上至介亭，亭左復有亭曰極目，曰蕭森，右復有亭曰麗雲、半山。

translations.literal: Again by the ridge path one ascended to Jie Pavilion; left of the pavilion was again a pavilion called Jimu, Xiaosen; right again pavilions Liyun, Banshan.
translations.idiomatic: Again by the ridge path one ascended to Jie Pavilion; to its left stood Jimu and Xiaosen pavilions; to its right, Liyun and Banshan pavilions.

sentences.zh: 北俯景龍江，引江之上流注山間。

translations.literal: North overlooking Jinglong River, the river's upper course was led to flow among the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: To the north one overlooked Jinglong River, whose upper course was channeled to flow among the mountains.

sentences.zh: 西行為漱瓊軒，又行石間為煉丹、凝觀、圜山亭，下視江際，見高陽酒肆及清澌閣。

translations.literal: Westward was Shuqiong Pavilion; again walking among stones was Liandan, Ningguan, and Yuanshan pavilions; looking down at the river's edge, one saw Gaoyang Wine Shop and Qingsi Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Westward lay Shuqiong Pavilion; farther along the stones stood the Liandan, Ningguan, and Yuanshan pavilions; looking down to the river's edge one could see Gaoyang Wine Shop and Qingsi Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 北岸有勝筠庵、躡雲台、蕭閑館、飛岑亭。

translations.literal: On the north bank were Shengyun Hermitage, Nieyun Platform, Xiaoxian Lodge, and Feicen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the north bank stood Shengyun Hermitage, Nieyun Platform, Xiaoxian Lodge, and Feicen Pavilion.

translations.literal: Branch streams separately formed a mountain estate and a winding stream.
translations.idiomatic: Branch streams separately formed a mountain estate and a winding stream.

sentences.zh: 又于南山之外為小山，橫亙二里，曰芙蓉城，窮極巧妙。

translations.literal: Again outside the south mountain a small hill was made, spanning two li, called Furong City, ingenious to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Again, beyond the south mountain a small hill was raised, spanning two li, called Furong City, ingenious to the utmost degree.

sentences.zh: 而景龍江外，則諸館舍尤精。

translations.literal: Outside Jinglong River, the various lodges were especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Jinglong River, the various lodges were especially refined.

sentences.zh: 其北又因瑤華宮火，取其地作大池，名曰曲江，池中有堂曰蓬壺，東盡封丘門而止。

translations.literal: To its north, again because of a fire at Yaohua Palace, that land was taken to make a great pool called Qujiang; within the pool was a hall called Penghu, extending east to Fengqiu Gate and stopping there.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, again after a fire at Yaohua Palace, that ground was taken to fashion a great pool named Qujiang; within the pool stood a hall called Penghu, running east as far as Fengqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 其西則自天波門橋引水直西，殆半裏，江乃折南，又折北。

translations.literal: To its west, water was drawn from the Tianbo Gate bridge straight west for nearly half a li; the channel then turned south, then turned north again.
translations.idiomatic: On the west, water was led from the Tianbo Gate bridge due west for nearly half a li; the stream then bent south, then bent north again.

sentences.zh: 折南者過閶闔門，為復道，通茂德帝姬宅。

translations.literal: The southward bend passed Changhe Gate, forming an elevated passageway that connected to the residence of the Princess of Maode.
translations.idiomatic: Where it bent south it passed Changhe Gate, where an elevated walkway was built linking to the residence of the Princess of Maode.

sentences.zh: 折北者四五里，屬之龍德宮。

translations.literal: The northward bend ran four or five li and joined Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Where it bent north it ran four or five li and was joined to Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，徽宗自為《艮嶽記》，以為山在國之艮，故名艮嶽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, Huizong himself wrote "Record of Genyue," holding that the mountain stood in the gen (northeast) quarter of the realm, and therefore named it Genyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, Huizong personally composed the "Record of Genyue," reasoning that the mountain occupied the gen (northeast) position of the realm and naming it Genyue.

sentences.zh: 蔡條謂初名鳳凰山，後神降，其詩有「艮嶽排空霄」，因改名艮嶽。

translations.literal: Cai Tiao said that at first it was called Phoenix Mountain; later, when a spirit descended, its verse included "Genyue towers into the empty skies," and it was renamed Genyue.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tiao stated that at first it was called Phoenix Mountain; later a spirit descended, and in its verse was the line "Genyue towers into the empty skies," whereupon the name Genyue was adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，詔以金芝產于艮岳之萬壽峰，又改名壽嶽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe, an edict noted that a golden fungus had appeared on Wanshou Peak of Genyue, and it was again renamed Shouyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuanhe, an edict declared that a golden fungus had sprung up on Wanshou Peak of Genyue, and the mount was renamed again as Shouyue.

sentences.zh: 蔡絛謂南山成，又改名壽嶽。

translations.literal: Cai Jie said that when the south mountain was completed, it was again renamed Shouyue.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jie said that when the south mountain was finished, it was again renamed Shouyue.

sentences.zh: 岳之正門名曰陽華，故亦號陽華宮。

translations.literal: The main gate of the mount was called Yanghua, so it was also styled Yanghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The mount's main gate was named Yanghua, and it was also called Yanghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 自政和訖靖康，積累十餘年，四方花竹奇石，悉聚於斯，樓臺亭館，雖略如前所記，而月增日益，殆不可以數計。

translations.literal: From Zhenghe through Jingkang, accumulated over more than ten years, flowers, bamboo, and strange stones from the four quarters were all gathered here; towers, terraces, and lodges, though roughly as previously recorded, grew month by month and day by day until they could scarcely be counted.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenghe era through Jingkang, over more than ten years of accumulation, flowers, bamboo, and curious stones from every direction were all assembled here; pavilions, towers, and lodges, though only broadly as noted before, increased month by month and day by day until they could hardly be numbered.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，朱勔於太湖取石，高廣數丈，載以大舟，挽以千夫，鑿河斷橋，毀堰拆閘，數月乃至，賜號「昭功敷慶神運石」，是年，初得燕地故也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe, Zhu Mian took stone from Taihu Lake, several zhang in height and breadth; it was loaded on a great boat and hauled by a thousand men; rivers were cut, bridges broken, dams destroyed, and sluice gates dismantled; only after several months did it arrive, and it was granted the name "Stone of Divine Transport Proclaiming Merit and Spreading Blessings"—in that year they had first taken the Yan territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuanhe, Zhu Mian quarried stone from Taihu Lake several zhang high and wide; it was borne on a great vessel and towed by a thousand laborers, with canals cut, bridges severed, dams ruined, and locks torn down; only after many months did it arrive, receiving the title "Stone of Divine Transport Proclaiming Merit and Spreading Blessings"—that year being when the Yan lands were first won.

translations.literal: Because of this, Mian was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this Mian was made a military commissioner.

translations.literal: In general the eunuch faction would not cease provoking construction.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part the cluster of eunuchs would not stop launching building projects.

sentences.zh: 徽宗晚歲，患苑囿之眾，國力不能支，數有厭惡語，由是得稍止。

translations.literal: In his later years Huizong grew troubled that the parks were too many and the state's strength could not sustain them; he uttered disgust several times, and thereby construction was able to ease somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Huizong fretted that the imperial parks had grown beyond what national strength could bear and repeatedly spoke of his weariness, so that construction was able to slacken somewhat.

sentences.zh: 及金人再至，圍城日久，欽宗命取山禽水鳥十余萬。

translations.literal: When the Jin came again and the siege dragged on, Qinzong ordered that more than a hundred thousand mountain birds and waterfowl be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin returned and the siege wore on, Qinzong ordered more than a hundred thousand mountain birds and waterfowl seized.

translations.literal: All were cast into the Bian River and left to go where they would.
translations.idiomatic: All were thrown into the Bian River and allowed to go wherever they might.

sentences.zh: 拆屋為新，鑿石為炮，伐竹為笓籬。

translations.literal: Buildings were torn down for fuel, stone was quarried for cannon, and bamboo was felled for palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Halls were dismantled for firewood, stone was hewn for cannon, and bamboo was cut for palisade fencing.

sentences.zh: 又取大鹿數百千頭殺之，以啖衛士雲。

translations.literal: Again several hundred or a thousand great deer were taken and killed to feed the guards, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred or a thousand great deer were also taken and slaughtered to feed the guards, it was said.

sentences.zh: 舊城周回二十里一百五十五步。

translations.literal: The old city had a circuit of twenty li and one hundred fifty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: The old city measured twenty li and one hundred fifty-five paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 東二門：北曰望春，宋初名和政。

translations.literal: On the east were two gates: the north was called Wangchun; in early Song it had been named Hezheng.
translations.idiomatic: East, two gates: the north was called Wangchun; in the early Song it had been named Hezheng.

translations.literal: The south was called Lijing.
translations.idiomatic: The south was called Lijing.

sentences.zh: 南面三門：中曰朱雀，東曰保康，大中祥符五年創建。

translations.literal: On the south face were three gates: the center was called Zhuque; the east was called Baokang, created in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: On the south were three gates: the center was Zhuque; the east was Baokang, established in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

translations.literal: The west was called Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: The west was called Chongming.

sentences.zh: 西二門：南曰宜秋，北曰閶闔。

translations.literal: On the west were two gates: the south was called Yiqiu; the north was called Changhe.
translations.idiomatic: West, two gates: the south was Yiqiu; the north was Changhe.

sentences.zh: 北三門：中曰景龍，東曰安遠，西曰天波。

translations.literal: On the north were three gates: the center was Jinglong; the east was Anyuan; the west was Tianbo.
translations.idiomatic: North, three gates: the center was Jinglong; the east was Anyuan; the west was Tianbo.

sentences.zh: 以上宋初仍梁、晉舊名，至太平興國四年改今名。

translations.literal: The above in early Song still bore the old names of Liang and Jin; in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo they were changed to the present names.
translations.idiomatic: These in early Song still used the old names of Liang and Jin; in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo they were given their present names.

sentences.zh: 新城周回五十里百六十五步。

translations.literal: The new city had a circuit of fifty li and one hundred sixty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: The new city measured fifty li and one hundred sixty-five paces in circumference.
