sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年增築，元豐元年重修，政和六年，詔有司度國之南展築京城，移置官司軍營。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu it was enlarged; in the first year of Yuanfeng it was renovated; in the sixth year of Zhenghe an edict ordered the relevant offices to measure southward and extend the capital walls, relocating government offices and military camps.
translations.idiomatic: It was enlarged in the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu and renovated in the first year of Yuanfeng; in the sixth year of Zhenghe an edict directed the authorities to survey southward, extend the capital walls, and relocate government offices and army camps.

sentences.zh: 舊城週四十八里二百三十三步，周顯德三年築。

translations.literal: The old city circuit was forty-eight li and two hundred thirty-three paces; it was built in the third year of Xiande of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The old city ran forty-eight li and two hundred thirty-three paces; it was built in the third year of Xiande of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 南三門：中曰南薰，東曰宣化，西曰安上。

translations.literal: On the south were three gates: the center was Nanxun; the east was Xuanhua; the west was Anshang.
translations.idiomatic: South, three gates: the center was Nanxun; the east was Xuanhua; the west was Anshang.

sentences.zh: 東二門：南曰朝陽，北曰含輝。

translations.literal: On the east were two gates: the south was Chaoyang; the north was Hanhui.
translations.idiomatic: East, two gates: the south was Chaoyang; the north was Hanhui.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年改寅賓，後復。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo it was changed to Yinbin, then later restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo it was renamed Yinbin, then later restored.

sentences.zh: 西二門：南曰順天，北曰金耀。

translations.literal: On the west were two gates: the south was Shuntian; the north was Jinyao.
translations.idiomatic: West, two gates: the south was Shuntian; the north was Jinyao.

sentences.zh: 北四門：中曰通天，天聖初改寧德，後復。

translations.literal: On the north were four gates: the center was Tongtian; at the start of Tiansheng it was changed to Ningde, then later restored.
translations.idiomatic: North, four gates: the center was Tongtian; at the beginning of Tiansheng it was renamed Ningde, then later restored.

sentences.zh: 東曰長景，次東曰永泰，西曰安肅。

translations.literal: To the east was Changjing; next east was Yongtai; to the west was Ansuo.
translations.idiomatic: East was Changjing; next east was Yongtai; west was Ansuo.

translations.literal: At first it was called Weizhou Gate.
translations.idiomatic: It was first called Weizhou Gate.

sentences.zh: 以上皆因周舊名，至太平興國四年，改今名。

translations.literal: The above all followed Zhou old names; in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo they were changed to the present names.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above followed Zhou-era names; in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo they were changed to the present names.

sentences.zh: 汴河上水門，南曰大通，太平興國四年賜名，天聖初，改順濟，後復今名。

translations.literal: Bian River upper sluice gate: the south was Datong, name granted in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo; at the start of Tiansheng it was changed to Shunji, then later restored to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: On the Bian River, the upper water gate to the south was Datong, a name granted in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo; at the beginning of Tiansheng it was changed to Shunji, then later restored to the present name.

translations.literal: The north was Xuanze.
translations.idiomatic: The north was Xuanze.

sentences.zh: 舊南北水門皆曰大通，熙寧十年改。

translations.literal: Formerly both north and south water gates were called Datong; they were changed in the tenth year of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly both north and south water gates had been called Datong; in the tenth year of Xining they were changed.

sentences.zh: 汴河下，南曰上善，北曰通津。

translations.literal: On the lower Bian River, the south was Shangshan and the north was Tongjin.
translations.idiomatic: On the lower Bian River, the south was Shangshan and the north was Tongjin.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，改廣津，熙寧十年復。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiansheng they were changed to Guangjin; in the tenth year of Xining they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiansheng they were changed to Guangjin; in the tenth year of Xining they were restored.

sentences.zh: 惠民河，上曰普濟，下曰廣利。

translations.literal: On the Huimin River, the upper gate was Puji and the lower was Guangli.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huimin River, the upper was Puji and the lower Guangli.

sentences.zh: 廣濟河，上曰咸豐，下曰善利，舊名咸通。

translations.literal: On the Guangji River, the upper was Xianfeng and the lower Shanli; the old name was Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: On the Guangji River, the upper was Xianfeng and the lower Shanli; the former name was Xiantong.

translations.literal: The upper south gate was called Yongshun.
translations.idiomatic: The upper south gate was called Yongshun.

translations.literal: The name was granted in the tenth year of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Its name was granted in the tenth year of Xining.

sentences.zh: 其後又于金耀門南置開遠門。

translations.literal: Later, south of Jinyao Gate, Kaiyuan Gate was additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kaiyuan Gate was also set up south of Jinyao Gate.

translations.literal: Its old name was Tongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Its former name was Tongyuan.

sentences.zh: 以上皆太平興國四年賜名，天聖初改今名。

translations.literal: All the above were names granted in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo; at the start of Tiansheng they were changed to the present names.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were names granted in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo; at the beginning of Tiansheng they were changed to the present names.

translations.literal: Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 唐顯慶間為東都，開元改河南府，宋為西京，山陵在焉。

translations.literal: Between the Xianqing years of Tang it was the Eastern Capital; in Kaiyuan it was changed to Henan Prefecture; under Song it was the Western Capital, and the imperial tombs were there.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era of Tang it served as Eastern Capital; in Kaiyuan it became Henan Prefecture; under Song it was the Western Capital, where the imperial tombs lay.

translations.literal: The palace city had a circuit of nine li and three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city measured nine li and three hundred paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 城南三門：中曰五鳳樓，東曰興教，西曰光政。

translations.literal: On the south of the palace city were three gates: the center was Wufeng Tower; the east was Xingjiao; the west was Guangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: South of the palace city were three gates: the center was Wufeng Tower; the east was Xingjiao; the west was Guangzheng.

translations.literal: These followed Sui and Tang old names.
translations.idiomatic: These followed Sui and Tang-era names.

translations.literal: On the east was one gate, called Canglong.
translations.idiomatic: East, one gate, called Canglong.

translations.literal: On the west was one gate, called Jinhu.
translations.idiomatic: West, one gate, called Jinhu.

translations.literal: On the north was one gate, called Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: North, one gate, called Gongchen.

sentences.zh: 舊名玄武，大中祥符五年改。

translations.literal: Its old name was Xuanwu; it was changed in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Its former name was Xuanwu; it was changed in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 五鳳樓內，東西門曰左、右永泰，門外道北有鸞和門，太平興國三年，以車輅院門改。

translations.literal: Inside Wufeng Tower, the east and west gates were called Left and Right Yongtai; north of the road outside the gate was Luanhe Gate; in the third year of Taiping Xingguo it was changed from the Cheluo Courtyard gate.
translations.idiomatic: Within Wufeng Tower, the east and west gates were Left and Right Yongtai; north of the road outside the gate stood Luanhe Gate, which in the third year of Taiping Xingguo had been converted from the Cheluo Courtyard gate.

translations.literal: West of Right Yongtai Gate was Yongfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: West of Right Yongtai Gate was Yongfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 興教、光政門內各三門，曰：左、右安禮，左、右興善，左、右銀台。

translations.literal: Inside Xingjiao and Guangzheng gates were three gates each, called: Left and Right Anli, Left and Right Xingshan, and Left and Right Yintai.
translations.idiomatic: Within Xingjiao and Guangzheng gates were three gates apiece, named Left and Right Anli, Left and Right Xingshan, and Left and Right Yintai.

sentences.zh: 蒼龍、金虎門內第二隔門曰膺福、千秋。

translations.literal: Inside Canglong and Jinhu gates the second inner gates were Yingfu and Qianqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Canglong and Jinhu gates the second partition gates were Yingfu and Qianqiu.

sentences.zh: 膺福門內道北門曰建禮。

translations.literal: Inside Yingfu Gate, the gate north on the inner road was called Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: Within Yingfu Gate, the gate to the north on the inner road was called Jianli.

sentences.zh: 正殿曰太極，舊名明堂，太平興國三年改。

translations.literal: The main hall was called Taiji; its old name was Mingtang; it was changed in the third year of Taiping Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The principal hall was Taiji; formerly it had been called Mingtang and was renamed in the third year of Taiping Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 殿前有日、月樓、日華、月華門，又有三門，曰太極殿門。

translations.literal: Before the hall were the Sun and Moon towers and the Rihua and Yuehua gates, and again three gates called Taiji Hall Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before the hall stood the Sun and Moon towers and the Rihua and Yuehua gates, and three further gates called Taiji Hall Gate.

sentences.zh: 後有殿曰天興，次北殿曰武德。

translations.literal: Behind was a hall called Tianxing; next to the north was a hall called Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Behind stood Tianxing Hall; next north was Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 西有門三重，曰：應天、乾元、敷政。

translations.literal: To the west were three sets of gates, called Yingtian, Qianyuan, and Fuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: To the west were three gate complexes: Yingtian, Qianyuan, and Fuzheng.

sentences.zh: 內有文明殿，旁有東上閣門、西上閣門，前有左、右延福門。

translations.literal: Inside was Wenhua Hall; beside it were East Upper Pavilion Gate and West Upper Pavilion Gate; before it were Left and Right Yanfu Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Within lay Wenhua Hall, flanked by East Upper Pavilion Gate and West Upper Pavilion Gate, with Left and Right Yanfu Gates before it.

sentences.zh: 後又有殿曰垂拱，殿北有通天門，柱廊北有明福門，門內有天福殿，殿北有寢殿曰太清，第二殿曰思政，第三殿曰延春。

translations.literal: Behind was again a hall called Chuigong; north of the hall was Tongtian Gate; north of the columned corridor was Mingfu Gate; inside the gate was Tianfu Hall; north of the hall were sleeping halls: the first called Taiqing, the second Sizheng, the third Yanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Farther back was Chuigong Hall; north of the hall stood Tongtian Gate; north of the columned corridor was Mingfu Gate; within the gate was Tianfu Hall; north of the hall were residential halls named Taiqing, then Sizheng, then Yanchun.

sentences.zh: 東又有廣壽殿，視朝之所也。

translations.literal: To the east was also Guangshou Hall, the place for holding court.
translations.idiomatic: To the east was also Guangshou Hall, where audiences were held.

sentences.zh: 北第二殿曰明德，第三殿曰天和，第四殿曰崇徽。

translations.literal: To the north, the second hall was Mingde, the third Tianhe, and the fourth Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Northward, the second hall was Mingde, the third Tianhe, and the fourth Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 天福殿西有金鸞殿，對殿南廊有彰善門。

translations.literal: West of Tianfu Hall was Jinluan Hall; on the south corridor facing the hall was Zhangshan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: West of Tianfu Hall stood Jinluan Hall; on the south corridor opposite the hall was Zhangshan Gate.

sentences.zh: 殿北第二殿曰壽昌，第三殿曰玉華，第四殿曰長壽，第五殿曰甘露，第六殿曰乾陽，第七殿曰善興。

translations.literal: North of the hall, the second hall was Shouchang, the third Yuhua, the fourth Changshou, the fifth Ganlu, the sixth Qianyang, and the seventh Shanxing.
translations.idiomatic: North of the hall came Shouchang as the second hall, Yuhua as the third, Changshou as the fourth, Ganlu as the fifth, Qianyang as the sixth, and Shanxing as the seventh.

translations.literal: To the west was an archery hall.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was an archery hall.

translations.literal: Inside Qianqiu Gate was Hanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Qianqiu Gate stood Hanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 拱宸門內西偏有保寧門，門內有講武殿，北又有殿相對。

translations.literal: Inside Gongchen Gate on the west side was Baoning Gate; within the gate was Jiangwu Hall, and to the north were paired halls.
translations.idiomatic: Within Gongchen Gate on the west flank was Baoning Gate; inside it stood Jiangwu Hall, with paired halls to the north.

sentences.zh: 內園有長春殿、淑景亭、十字亭、九江池、砌台、娑羅亭。

translations.literal: The inner garden had Changchun Hall, Shujing Pavilion, Shizi Pavilion, Jiujiang Pool, Qitai, and Suoluo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The inner garden contained Changchun Hall, Shujing Pavilion, Shizi Pavilion, Jiujiang Pool, Qitai, and Suoluo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宮城東西有夾城，各三里餘。

translations.literal: East and west of the palace city were barrier walls, each more than three li long.
translations.idiomatic: East and west of the palace city ran barrier walls, each over three li in length.

sentences.zh: 東二門：南曰賓曜，北曰啟明。

translations.literal: On the east were two gates: the south was Binyao; the north was Qiming.
translations.idiomatic: East, two gates: the south was Binyao; the north was Qiming.

sentences.zh: 西二門：南曰金曜，北曰乾通。

translations.literal: On the west were two gates: the south was Jinyao; the north was Qiantong.
translations.idiomatic: West, two gates: the south was Jinyao; the north was Qiantong.

sentences.zh: 宮室合九千九百九十余區。

translations.literal: Palace buildings in all numbered more than nine thousand nine hundred and ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Palace structures totaled more than nine thousand nine hundred and ninety bays.

sentences.zh: 夾城內及內城北，皆左右禁軍所處。

translations.literal: Within the barrier walls and north of the inner city were quarters of the Left and Right Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Within the barrier walls and north of the inner city lay the encampments of the Left and Right Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 皇城周回十八里二百五十八步。

translations.literal: The imperial city had a circuit of eighteen li and two hundred fifty-eight paces.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial city measured eighteen li and two hundred fifty-eight paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 南面三門：中曰端門，東西曰左、右掖門。

translations.literal: On the south were three gates: the center was Duanmen; east and west were Left and Right Yemen.
translations.idiomatic: South, three gates: the center was Duanmen; east and west were Left and Right Yemen.

translations.literal: On the east was one gate, called Xuanren.
translations.idiomatic: East, one gate, called Xuanren.

sentences.zh: 西三門：南曰麗景，與金曜相直，中曰開化，與乾通相直；

translations.literal: On the west were three gates: the south was Lijing, aligned with Jinyao; the center was Kaihua, aligned with Qiantong;
translations.idiomatic: West, three gates: the south was Lijing, opposite Jinyao; the center was Kaihua, opposite Qiantong;

translations.literal: the north was Yingfu.
translations.idiomatic: the north was Yingfu.

translations.literal: Inside were the quarters of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: Within were the quarters of the various government offices.

sentences.zh: 京城週五十二里九十六步。

translations.literal: The capital city measured fifty-two li and ninety-six paces in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city measured fifty-two li and ninety-six paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 隋大業元年築，唐長壽二年增築。

translations.literal: It was built in the first year of Daye of Sui and enlarged in the second year of Changshou of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: It was built in the first year of Daye of Sui and enlarged in the second year of Changshou of Tang.

translations.literal: Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，建應天府為南京。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Yingtian Prefecture was established as the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Yingtian Prefecture was made the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 宮城週二里三百一十六步。

translations.literal: The palace city measured two li and three hundred sixteen paces in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city measured two li and three hundred sixteen paces in circumference.

translations.literal: The gates were Chongxi and Banqing.
translations.idiomatic: Its gates were Chongxi and Banqing.

translations.literal: The hall was called Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Its hall was called Guide.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，賜度僧牒修外城門及西橋等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, ordination certificates for monks were granted to repair the outer city gates and the west bridge and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, ordination certificates were issued to fund repairs to the outer city gates, the west bridge, and similar works.

sentences.zh: 京城周回一十五里四十步。

translations.literal: The capital city had a circuit of fifteen li and forty paces.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city measured fifteen li and forty paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 東二門：南曰延和，北曰昭仁。

translations.literal: On the east were two gates: the south was Yanhe; the north was Zhaoren.
translations.idiomatic: East, two gates: the south was Yanhe; the north was Zhaoren.

sentences.zh: 西二門：南曰順成，北曰回鑾。

translations.literal: On the west were two gates: the south was Shuncheng; the north was Huiluan.
translations.idiomatic: West, two gates: the south was Shuncheng; the north was Huiluan.

translations.literal: On the south was one gate, called Chongli.
translations.idiomatic: South, one gate, called Chongli.

translations.literal: On the north was one gate, called Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: North, one gate, called Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 中有隔城，又有門二：東曰承慶，西曰祥輝。

translations.literal: Within was a partition city, and again two gates: east was Chengqing; west was Xianghui.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood a partition city with two more gates: east, Chengqing; west, Xianghui.

sentences.zh: 其東又有關城，南北各一門。

translations.literal: To its east was also a barrier city, with one gate each on south and north.
translations.idiomatic: East of it lay another barrier city, one gate on the south and one on the north.

translations.literal: Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，建大名府為北京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Daming Superior Prefecture was established as the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli (1042), Daming Superior Prefecture was made the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 宮城週三里一百九十八步，即真宗駐蹕行宮。

translations.literal: The palace city had a circuit of three li and one hundred ninety-eight paces; it was the traveling palace where Emperor Zhenzong halted the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city measured three li and one hundred ninety-eight paces around—the traveling palace where Emperor Zhenzong had halted on campaign.

sentences.zh: 城南三門：中曰順豫，東曰省風，西曰展義。

translations.literal: On the south of the city were three gates: the center was Shunyu; east was Shengfeng; west was Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city, three gates: the center, Shunyu; east, Shengfeng; west, Zhanyi.

translations.literal: On the east was one gate, called Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: East, one gate, called Dong'an.

translations.literal: On the west was one gate, called Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: West, one gate, called Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 順豫門內東西各一門，曰左、右保成。

translations.literal: Within Shunyu Gate, east and west each had one gate, called Left and Right Baocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Shunyu Gate, one gate east and one west, called Left and Right Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 次北班瑞殿，殿前東西門二：東曰凝祥，西曰麗澤。

translations.literal: Next north was the Banrui Hall; before the hall were two gates east and west: east was Ningxiang; west was Lize.
translations.idiomatic: North of that stood Banrui Hall; before it two gates, east Ningxiang and west Lize.

sentences.zh: 殿東南時巡殿門，次北時巡殿，次靖方殿，次慶寧殿。

translations.literal: Southeast of the hall was the Shixun Hall Gate; next north were the Shixun Hall, then the Jingfang Hall, then the Qingning Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the hall was the Shixun Hall gate; farther north came Shixun Hall, then Jingfang Hall, then Qingning Hall.

sentences.zh: 時巡殿前東西門二：東曰景清，西曰景和。

translations.literal: Before the Shixun Hall were two gates east and west: east was Jingqing; west was Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shixun Hall, two gates: east Jingqing, west Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 京城週四十八里二百六步，門一十七。

translations.literal: The capital city had a circuit of forty-eight li and two hundred six paces, with seventeen gates.
translations.idiomatic: The capital city measured forty-eight li and two hundred six paces around, with seventeen gates.

sentences.zh: 熙甯九年，改正南南河門曰景風，南磚曰亨嘉，鼓角曰阜昌。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining, the due-south Nanhe Gate was renamed Jingfeng; the south brick gate was renamed Hengjia; the drum-and-horn gate was renamed Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xining (1076), the due-south Nanhe Gate became Jingfeng, the south brick gate Hengjia, and the drum-and-horn gate Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 正北北河門曰安平，北磚曰耀德。

translations.literal: The due-north Beihe Gate was renamed Anping; the north brick gate was renamed Yaode.
translations.idiomatic: Due north, Beihe Gate became Anping and the north brick gate Yaode.

sentences.zh: 正東冠氏門曰華景，冠氏第二重曰春祺，子城東曰泰通。

translations.literal: The due-east Guanshi Gate was renamed Huajing; the second Guanshi gate was renamed Chunqi; the east of the inner city was renamed Taitong.
translations.idiomatic: Due east, Guanshi Gate became Huajing, its inner gate Chunqi, and the inner city's east gate Taitong.

sentences.zh: 正西魏縣門曰寶成，魏縣第二重曰利和，子城西曰宣澤。

translations.literal: The due-west Weixian Gate was renamed Baocheng; the second Weixian gate was renamed Lihe; the west of the inner city was renamed Xuanze.
translations.idiomatic: Due west, Weixian Gate became Baocheng, its inner gate Lihe, and the inner city's west gate Xuanze.

sentences.zh: 東南朝城門曰安流，朝城第二重曰巽齊。

translations.literal: The southeast Chaocheng Gate was renamed Anliu; the second Chaocheng gate was renamed Xunqi.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast, Chaocheng Gate became Anliu and its inner gate Xunqi.

sentences.zh: 西南觀音門曰安正，觀音第二重曰靜方。

translations.literal: The southwest Guanyin Gate was renamed Anzheng; the second Guanyin gate was renamed Jingfang.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest, Guanyin Gate became Anzheng and its inner gate Jingfang.

sentences.zh: 上水關曰善利，下水關曰永濟。

translations.literal: The upper water pass was called Shanli; the lower water pass was called Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: The upper water pass was Shanli; the lower, Yongji.

translations.literal: On the inner city a north gate was newly established, called Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The inner city gained a new north gate, Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 鵩元豐七年，廢善利、永濟關。

translations.literal: Again, in the seventh year of Yuanfeng, the Shanli and Yongji passes were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng (1084), the Shanli and Yongji passes were abolished.

translations.literal: Traveling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling Palace.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年閏八月，高宗自建康如臨安，以州治為行宮。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the third year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong went from Jiankang to Lin'an and made the prefectural seat the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of the third year of Jianyan (1129), Emperor Gaozong traveled from Jiankang to Lin'an and turned the prefectural seat into his traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 宮室制度皆從簡省，不尚華飾。

translations.literal: Palace regulations all followed simplicity and economy, without esteem for ornate display.
translations.idiomatic: Palace arrangements were kept simple and plain, with no taste for lavish ornament.

sentences.zh: 垂拱、大慶、文德、紫宸、祥曦、集英六殿，隨事易名，實一殿。

translations.literal: The six halls—Chuigong, Daqing, Wende, Zichen, Xiangxi, and Jiying—changed names as occasion required; in fact they were one hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chuigong, Daqing, Wende, Zichen, Xiangxi, and Jiying—the six halls—were renamed as needed but were really a single hall.

sentences.zh: 重華、慈福、壽慈、壽康四宮，重壽、寧福二殿，隨時異額，實德壽一宮。

translations.literal: The four palaces—Chonghua, Cifu, Shouci, and Shoukang—and the two halls—Chongshou and Ningfu—received different titles from time to time; in fact they were one palace, Deshou.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua, Cifu, Shouci, Shoukang, Chongshou, and Ningfu bore shifting titles, but all were one palace, Deshou.

sentences.zh: 延和、崇政、復古、選德四殿，本射殿也。

translations.literal: The four halls—Yanhe, Chongzheng, Fugu, and Xuande—were originally the archery hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhe, Chongzheng, Fugu, and Xuande had begun as the archery hall.

sentences.zh: 慈寧殿，紹興九年，以太后有歸期建。

translations.literal: The Cining Hall was built in the ninth year of Shaoxing, when the empress dowager had a date set for her return.
translations.idiomatic: Cining Hall was built in the ninth year of Shaoxing (1139), when the empress dowager was expected to return.

sentences.zh: 欽先孝思殿，十五年建，在崇政殿東。

translations.literal: The Qinxian Xiaosi Hall was built in the fifteenth year, east of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Qinxian Xiaosi Hall was built in the fifteenth year (1145), east of Chongzheng Hall.

translations.literal: The Cuihan Hall was built by Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Cuihan Hall was built by Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 損齋，紹興末建，貯經史書，為燕坐之所。

translations.literal: The Sunzhai was built toward the end of the Shaoxing era; it stored the classics and histories and served as a place for leisurely sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Sunzhai was built late in Shaoxing to hold the classics and histories as a quiet retreat.

sentences.zh: 東宮，在麗正門內，孝宗、莊文、景獻、光宗皆常居之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace, inside the Lizheng Gate, was where Xiaozong, Zhuangwen, Jingxian, and Guangzong all regularly resided.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace lay inside Lizheng Gate; Xiaozong, Zhuangwen, Jingxian, and Guangzong all lived there in turn.

translations.literal: The Lecture Seat: the Zishan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lecture seat: Zishan Hall.

sentences.zh: 在行宮門內，因書院而作。

translations.literal: It stood within the traveling palace gates and was made from a former academy.
translations.idiomatic: It stood inside the traveling palace gates, converted from a former academy.

sentences.zh: 天章、龍圖、寶文、顯猷、徽猷、敷文、煥章、華文、寶謨九閣，實天章一閣。

translations.literal: The nine pavilions—Tianzhang, Longtu, Baowen, Xianyou, Huixuan, Fuwen, Huanzhang, Huawen, and Baomo—in fact were one pavilion, Tianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhang, Longtu, Baowen, Xianyou, Huixuan, Fuwen, Huanzhang, Huawen, and Baomo were nine names for one pavilion, Tianzhang.

translations.literal: Jingji Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingji Circuit.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，以京東之曹州，京西之陳、許、鄭、滑州為輔郡，隸畿內，並開封府，合四十二縣，置京畿路轉運使及提點刑獄總之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangyou, Caozhou of Jingdong and Chen, Xu, Zheng, and Huazhou of Jingxi were made auxiliary prefectures within the metropolitan zone, together with Kaifeng Superior Prefecture—forty-two counties in all—and a Jingji Circuit transport commissioner and judicial intendant were established to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangyou (1053), Caozhou in Jingdong and Chen, Xu, Zheng, and Hua in Jingxi became auxiliary prefectures of the inner circuit, joining Kaifeng—forty-two counties in all—and a Jingji transport commissioner and judicial intendant were appointed.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，罷京畿路轉運使、提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe, the Jingji Circuit transport commissioner and judicial intendant were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhihe (1055), the Jingji transport commissioner and judicial intendant were abolished.

sentences.zh: 其曹、陳、許、鄭、滑各隸本路，為輔郡如故。

translations.literal: Cao, Chen, Xu, Zheng, and Hua each reverted to their original circuits, remaining auxiliary prefectures as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao, Chen, Xu, Zheng, and Hua returned to their home circuits but stayed auxiliary prefectures.

sentences.zh: 崇甯四年，京畿路復置轉運使及提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning, the Jingji Circuit transport commissioner and judicial intendant were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongning (1105), the Jingji transport commissioner and judicial intendant were restored.

sentences.zh: 先是，改開封府界為京畿路，是年，又於京畿四面置四輔郡：潁昌府為南輔，鄭州為西輔，澶州為北輔，建拱州於開封襄邑縣為東輔，並屬京畿。
